paras.t: Tulit ergo rex annulum quo utebatur, non solum ad manus suæ ornatum, sed item ad litteras sigillandas, sicut tunc moris fuit. In annulis demum talibus fuit signum formatum ad imprimendum et signandum epistolas. De manu sua, et dedit eum Aman, ut juxta suum conceptum dictaret et sigillaret ex nomine regis litteras mortis contra Judæos. Credidit Assuerus nimis impio Aman, non inquirens accusationis veritatem. Facilitas autem credulitatis decipit multos, et in præsidentibus periculosa est subditis, etiam bonis.
paras.en: [[3:10|And the king took the ring that he used|Tulit ergo rex annulum quo utebatur]], not only to adorn his hand but also to seal letters, as was then the custom; for in such rings a device was cut for impressing and sealing letters. [[3:10|from his own hand, and gave it to Aman|De manu sua, et dedit eum Aman]], that he might dictate according to his own design, and seal in the king's name, letters of death against the Jews. Assuerus believed the most wicked Aman too readily, not inquiring into the truth of the accusation. Now readiness to believe deceives many, and in those who rule it is dangerous to their subjects, even to the good.

paras.t: Vocatique sunt scribæ, id est scriptores, regis. Scriba tamen frequenter accipitur pro sapiente seu doctore, vel legisperito.
paras.en: [[3:12|And the king's scribes were called|Vocatique sunt scribæ, id est scriptores, regis]]: *scribes*, that is, writers. Yet *scribe* is often taken for a wise man or teacher, or one learned in the law.

paras.t: Et litteræ missæ sunt per cursores regis ad universas provincias regni ejus, ut occiderent omnes Judæos a puero usque ad senem, id est universos, etiam infantulos atque decrepitos, et mulieres, id est cunctas personas feminei sexus. Et ut proniores essent gentiles hoc facere, dabatur facientibus illud licentia diripiendi ac retinendi bona Judæorum, quos trucidarent. Ideo subditur, et bona eorum diriperent. Sic quippe filii Israel vastaverunt Amalecitas: tamen contra præceptum Dei, pepercerunt pecoribus Amalec, sicut primo Regum fertur.
paras.en: [[3:12|and the letters|Et litteræ]] [[3:13|Were sent by the king's messengers to all provinces|missæ sunt per cursores regis ad universas provincias]] of his kingdom, [[3:13|to kill|ut occiderent]] [[3:13|all the Jews, both young and old|omnes Judæos a puero usque ad senem]], that is, all of them, even little infants and the decrepit, [[3:13|and women|et mulieres]], that is, all persons of the female sex. And that the gentiles might be the readier to do this, leave was given to those who did it to plunder and keep the goods of the Jews whom they slaughtered. Therefore it is added: [[3:13|and to make a spoil of their goods|et bona eorum diriperent]]. For so the children of Israel laid waste the Amalecites[[1 Kings 15:7||]]; yet, against the command of God, they spared the cattle of Amalec, as is told in the first book of Kings[[1 Kings 15:9||]].

paras.t: Statimque in Susis metropoli regni, pependit edictum: id est, ex dispositione Aman, appensum est decretum in scriptis de Judæorum interitu, ne rex suam revocaret sententiam, sicut nec eam de Vasthi abjectione revocare audebat. Hoc loco ponit Josephus formam epistolæ prætactæ ex nomine regis cunctis ejus provinciis missæ: quæ infra continetur. Rege et Aman celebrante convivium, tanquam rem communitati saluberrimam ordinassent, et cunctis Judæis qui in urbe Susis erant, flentibus: imo, ut Josephus scribit, etiam civitas turbabatur, utpote Judæis captivatis compatiens.
paras.en: [[3:15|And immediately the edict was hung up in Susan|Statimque in Susis metropoli regni, pependit edictum]], the capital of the kingdom: that is, by Aman's arrangement the decree concerning the destruction of the Jews was hung up in writing, lest the king should revoke his sentence, just as he did not dare to revoke the one on the casting off of Vasthi. At this place Josephus gives the form of the aforesaid letter sent in the king's name to all his provinces, which is contained further on[[Esth 13:1||]] [the margin reads "Esther xi, 1–7" as OCR'd; the letter is Esther 13:1–7]. [[3:15|the king and Aman feasting together|Rege et Aman celebrante convivium]], as though they had ordained something most wholesome for the community, [[3:15|and all the Jews that were in the city weeping|et cunctis Judæis qui in urbe Susis erant, flentibus]]: nay more, as Josephus writes, even the city was troubled, as having compassion on the Jews held captive.

4.title: Expositio capituli quarti: Quæ quum audisset Mardochæus, scidit vestimenta sua
4.title_en: Exposition of the fourth chapter: Now when Mardochai had heard these things, he rent his garments

paras.t: Refertur hic, qualiter Mardochæus Esther reginam induxit ad intercedendum coram rege pro liberatione plebis Judaicæ.
paras.en: Here it is told how Mardochai induced Queen Esther to intercede before the king for the deliverance of the Jewish people.

paras.t: Quæ quum audisset Mardochæus, scidit vestimenta sua, ut moris fuit Judæis, imo et quibusdam gentilibus, sicut in libro Job, ipse Job et amici ejus leguntur vestimenta sua scidisse, et indutus est sacco, id est aspera saccinaque veste, in signum contritionis, spargens cinerem capiti, ad humiliandum se coram Deo, quasi pulverem se recognoscens ac cinerem; et in platea mediæ civitatis voce magna clamabat, ostendens amaritudinem animi sui: præsertim quia pensabat se esse occasionem tanti periculi, ac desolationis dijudicationisque populi sui; et hoc ejulatu usque ad fores, id est januas, palatii gradiens. Non enim erat licitum, indutum sacco aulam regis intrare. Unde secundum Josephum, usque ad aulam pervenit, et ante ipsam stetit: quam cum tali habitu ingredi, fuit prohibitum, ne hujuscemodi vestis, aut sic vestitus, miserabilisque apparens, horrorem incuteret regi, aut ejus magnificentiæ derogaret. In omnibus quoque provinciis, oppidis ac locis, ad quæ crudele regis dogma, id est præfatum edictum quasi doctrinaliter et apparenter dictatum, pervenerat, planctus ingens erat apud Judæos, plurimis sacco et cinere pro strato utentibus, ad impetrandum auxilium Dei, juxta illud Jeremiæ: Accingere cilicio, conspergere cinere.
paras.en: [[4:1|Now when Mardochai had heard these things, he rent his garments|Quæ quum audisset Mardochæus, scidit vestimenta sua]], as was the custom of the Jews, and indeed of some Gentiles, as in the book of Job we read that Job himself[[Job 1:20||]] and his friends[[Job 2:12||]] rent their garments; [[4:1|and put on sackcloth|et indutus est sacco]], that is, a rough garment of sacking, in sign of contrition, [[4:1|strewing ashes on his head|spargens cinerem capiti]], to humble himself before God, acknowledging himself to be as dust and ashes; [[4:1|and he cried with a loud voice in the street in the midst of the city, shewing the anguish of his mind|et in platea mediæ civitatis voce magna clamabat, ostendens amaritudinem animi sui]], especially because he reckoned that he was the occasion of so great a danger, and of the desolation and condemnation of his people; [[4:2|And he came lamenting in this manner even to the gate|et hoc ejulatu usque ad fores]], that is, the doors, [[4:2|of the palace|palatii gradiens]]: [[4:2|for no one clothed with sackcloth might enter the king's court|Non enim erat licitum, indutum sacco aulam regis intrare]]. Hence according to Josephus he came as far as the court and stood before it; for it was forbidden to enter it in such a dress, lest such a garment, or a man so clad and looking so wretched, should strike the king with horror, or detract from his magnificence. [[4:3|And in all provinces, towns, and places, to which the king's cruel edict was come|In omnibus quoque provinciis, oppidis, ac locis, ad quæ crudele regis dogma pervenerat]] (*dogma*, that is, the aforesaid edict, dictated as it were by way of doctrine and for show), [[4:3|there was great mourning among the Jews|planctus ingens erat apud Judæos]], [[4:3|many using sackcloth and ashes for their bed|plurimis sacco et cinere pro strato utentibus]], to obtain the help of God, according to the word of Jeremias: [[Jer 6:26|Gird thee with sackcloth|Accingere cilicio]], [[Jer 6:26|and sprinkle thee with ashes|conspergere cinere]] [the margin's reference is misread; the words are those of Jer 6:26].

paras.t: Ingressæ sunt autem puellæ Esther et eunuchi, id est pedisequæ ejus, et cubicularii qui erant castrati. Et apparet quod isti secrete noverunt Mardochæum et Esther esse cognatos. Nuntiaveruntque ei. Quod audiens Esther, consternata est, id est, mœrore oppressa; et misit vestem Mardochæo, ut indueret eam, sicque honeste vestitus, aulam intraret; quam accipere noluit Mardochæus, quia nondum finitum fuit malum illud pœnale, propter quod evadendum, induerat saccum. Accitoque Athach eunucho præcepit ut iret ad Mardochæum, et disceret cur hoc faceret. Egressusque Athach, invenit eum in platea civitatis: qui indicavit per eunuchum ei, scilicet Esther reginæ, omnia quæ acciderant in hoc casu, ut intraret ad regem, et deprecaretur pro populo suo. De quo faciendo excusat se, quia edictum fuit, quod quicumque non vocatus ingrederetur atrium regis, mox moreretur, nisi rex auream virgam quam tenebat in manu, ad sic introeuntem extenderet pro signo clementiæ. Hinc addidit: Ego igitur quomodo ad regem intrare potero, quæ triginta diebus non sum vocata ad eum? Habuit enim extra et alia multa deliciarum suarum objecta: et Deus omnipotens devotæ reginæ providit de tali continentia et quiete.
paras.en: [[4:4|Then Esther's maids and her eunuchs went in|Ingressæ sunt autem puellæ Esther et eunuchi]], that is, her waiting women, and the chamberlains who were castrated. And it appears that these secretly knew that Mardochai and Esther were kinsfolk. [[4:4|and told her|Nuntiaveruntque ei]]. [[4:4|And when she heard it she was in a consternation|Quod audiens Esther, consternata est]], that is, she was overwhelmed with grief; [[4:4|and she sent a garment|et misit vestem]] to Mardochai, for him to put on, so that, decently clad, he might enter the court; [[4:4|but he would not receive it|quam accipere noluit]], Mardochai, because that penal evil, to escape which he had put on sackcloth, was not yet ended. [[4:5|And she called for Athach the eunuch|Accitoque Athach eunucho]], [[4:5|and she commanded him to go to Mardochai, and learn|præcepit ut iret ad Mardochæum, et disceret]] [[4:5|why he did this|cur hoc faceret]]. [[4:6|And Athach going out|Egressusque Athach]] found him [[4:6|in the street of the city|in platea civitatis]]; [[4:7|And Mardochai told him all that had happened|qui indicavit ei omnia quæ acciderant]] through the eunuch, namely to Queen Esther, in this matter, [[4:8|and admonish her to go in to the king, and to entreat him for her people|ut intraret ad regem, et deprecaretur pro populo suo]]. She excuses herself from doing this, because it was decreed that whoever entered the king's court without being called should die at once, unless the king held out to one so entering the golden rod [*virga*: the Douay-Rheims has “sceptre”] which he held in his hand, in token of clemency. Hence she added: [[4:11|How then can I go in to the king, who for these thirty days now have not been called unto him?|Ego igitur quomodo ad regem intrare potero, quæ triginta diebus non sum vocata ad eum?]] For he had besides many other objects of his pleasures; and almighty God provided such continence and quiet for the devout queen.

paras.t: Quod quum audisset Mardochæus, rursus mandavit Esther reginæ, solita auctoritate loquens ad eam increpatorie et audacter, certus quod ipsa virtuosa domina patienter, non indignanter acciperet, dicens: Ne putes quod animam tuam tantum liberes, quia in domo es regis pro cunctis Judæis, id est, noli putare quod a sententia mortis contra Judæos promulgata, præserves propriam vitam dumtaxat per hoc, quod facta es contubernalis et conjux regis, et ideo non cures pro populo tuo rogare. Si enim nunc silueris, non rogando regem pro tuis, per aliam occasionem liberabuntur Judæi, id est, Deus aliis modis ac viis, eis (ut spero) succurret: et tu et domus tua peribitis, id est, Deus justo judicio permittet te, et domesticos seu cognatos tuos occidi, eo quod neglexeris populo tuo in tanto periculo subvenire. Et quis novit, utrum idcirco ad regnum perveneris, id est, consors et contoralis regis effecta sis, ut in tali tempore parareris, id est, ut disponaris venire ad prætactam ruinam in tempore persecutionis istius, in quo deseris tuos? Vel sensus est: Quis novit, etc.? ac si dicat: Quamvis occulta sint Dei judicia, forsitan tamen idcirco imperatrix et regina facta es, quatenus ex præordinatione divina pares te succurrere nobis.
paras.en: [[4:12|And when Mardochai had heard this|Quod quum audisset Mardochæus]], [[4:13|He sent word to Esther again|rursus mandavit Esther]], the queen, speaking to her with his wonted authority, in reproof and boldly, sure that the virtuous lady would take it patiently, not indignantly, [[4:13|saying: Think not that thou mayst save thy life only, because thou art in the king's house, more than all the Jews|dicens: Ne putes quod animam tuam tantum liberes, quia in domo es regis pro cunctis Judæis]] [Denis reads *pro*, “for”, where the Vulgate has *præ*, “more than”], that is, do not think that thou wilt save thy own life only from the sentence of death proclaimed against the Jews by this, that thou hast been made the king's companion and wife, and so care not to plead for thy people. [[4:14|For if thou wilt now hold thy peace|Si enim nunc silueris]], by not asking the king for thy own, [[4:14|the Jews shall be delivered by some other occasion|per aliam occasionem liberabuntur Judæi]], that is, God will help them (as I hope) in other ways and by other means; [[4:14|and thou|et tu]] and thy house [Denis reads *domus tua*, “thy house”, for the Vulgate's *domus patris tui*] [[4:14|shall perish|peribitis]], that is, God by a just judgement will allow thee and thy household or kinsfolk to be killed, because thou hast neglected to help thy people in so great a danger. [[4:14|And who knoweth whether thou art not therefore come to the kingdom|Et quis novit, utrum idcirco ad regnum perveneris]], that is, hast been made the king's consort and bedfellow, [[4:14|that thou mightest be ready in such a time as this?|ut in tali tempore parareris]] that is, that thou mayest be disposed to come to the ruin spoken of in the time of this persecution, in which thou forsakest thy own? Or the sense is: Who knoweth, etc.? as if he said: Though the judgements of God are hidden, yet perhaps thou hast been made empress and queen for this, that by divine preordaining thou mightest prepare thyself to help us.

paras.t: Rursumque Esther Mardochæo mandavit: Congrega omnes Judæos utriusque sexus, et orate pro me, ut communitatis oratio mihi prosperum mereatur successum. Non comedatis et non bibatis tribus diebus et tribus noctibus, nisi eo modo quo jejunantes solent non manducare, videlicet solum semel in die: vel tam parce et sobrie comedatis in die, ut quasi nil reputetur: sicut de eo qui parum comedit, dicimus, Nihil manducavit. Et ego cum ancillis meis similiter jejunabo. Sicque ancillæ istæ videntur fuisse fideles, et forsan conversæ per suam reginam. Et tunc ingrediar ad regem, sperando quod Deus misericorditer mecum disponet, et mentem regis mihi propitiam exhibebit, contra legem faciens, intrando ad regem invocata, id est non vocata, tradens me morti, id est periculo mortis, pro liberatione populi mei, nisi Deus gratiose provideat et succurrat. Ivit itaque Mardochæus ad exsequendum reginæ præceptum.
paras.en: [[4:15|And again Esther sent to Mardochai|Rursumque Esther Mardochæo mandavit]]: [[4:16|and gather together all the Jews|Congrega omnes Judæos]] of both sexes, [[4:16|and pray ye for me|et orate pro me]], so that the prayer of the community may win me good success. [[4:16|Neither eat nor drink for three days and three nights|Non comedatis et non bibatis tribus diebus et tribus noctibus]], except in the way in which those who fast are wont not to eat, namely once only in the day; or eat so sparingly and soberly in the day that it may count as almost nothing, as we say of one who has eaten little: He has eaten nothing. [[4:16|and I with my handmaids will fast in like manner|Et ego cum ancillis meis similiter jejunabo]]. And so these handmaids seem to have been of the faith, and perhaps converted by their queen. [[4:16|and then I will go in to the king|Et tunc ingrediar ad regem]], hoping that God will deal mercifully with me, and will make the king's mind favourable to me, [[4:16|against the law|contra legem faciens]], by going in to the king [[4:16|not being called|invocata]], that is, uncalled, [[4:16|and expose myself to death|tradens me morti]], that is, to the danger of death, for the deliverance of my people, unless God graciously provides and helps. [[4:17|So Mardochai went|Ivit itaque Mardochæus]] to carry out the queen's command.

5.title: Explanatio capituli quinti: Die autem tertio induta est Esther regalibus vestimentis
5.title_en: Explanation of the fifth chapter: And on the third day Esther put on her royal apparel

paras.t: Exordium petitionis Esther reginæ hic recitatur.
paras.en: Here the beginning of queen Esther's petition is related.

paras.t: Die autem tertio induta est Esther regalibus vestimentis: et sic regem accessisse videtur tertio die suæ jejunationis et orationis, orantibus adhuc pro ea, et jejunantibus cunctis Judæis in Susis manentibus. Ipsa quoque in lugubri veste oravit ac jejunavit: qua deposita, ornavit se pretiosissimis atque pulcherrimis quæ habuit vestimentis. Propter quod infra legitur, quod circumdata est gloria sua, et deposuit vestimenta ornatus sui: quia et communia ornamenta seu quotidiana vestimenta, quamvis pretiosa et decora, deposuit; vestimenta quoque lugubria, in quibus interiori ornatui, scilicet compunctioni, orationi, jejunationi vacavit. Et stetit in atrio, id est, a camera sua processit usque ad atrium, domus regiæ, quod erat interius contra basilicam, id est ex opposito regiæ aulæ. At ille sedebat super solium suum in consistorio, id est loco judicii ubi ad judicium statur, palatii, contra ostium domus, in qua rex sedit, ex qua potuit eam videre. Et antequam venit ad illum locum, ivit per januas multas, secundum quod infra legitur: Ingressa cuncta per ordinem ostia, etc.
paras.en: [[5:1|And on the third day Esther put on her royal apparel|Die autem tertio induta est Esther regalibus vestimentis]]: and so she seems to have gone to the king on the third day of her fasting and prayer, while all the Jews dwelling in Susa were still praying and fasting for her. She herself also prayed and fasted in mourning garments; and laying these aside, she adorned herself with the most precious and most beautiful garments that she had. For which reason it is read further on that she [[Esth 15:4|put on her glorious apparel|circumdata est gloria sua]] [literally "she was clothed about with her glory"], and [[Esth 15:4|laid away the garments she wore|deposuit vestimenta ornatus sui]] [literally "the garments of her adornment"]: because she laid aside both her common ornaments or everyday garments, precious and comely though they were, and also the mourning garments in which she had given herself to the inner adornment, that is, to compunction, prayer and fasting. [[5:1|and stood in the inner court|Et stetit in atrio]], that is, she went from her chamber as far as the court [[5:1|of the king's house|domus regiæ]], which was within, [[5:1|over against the king's hall|contra basilicam]], that is, opposite the royal hall. [[5:1|now he sat upon his throne|At ille sedebat super solium suum]] [[5:1|in the hall|in consistorio]], that is, in the place of judgment, where one stands to be judged, [[5:1|of the palace, over against the door of the house|palatii, contra ostium domus]] in which the king sat, from which he could see her. And before she came to that place she went through many doors, as is read further on: [[Esth 15:9|going in she passed through all doors in order|Ingressa cuncta per ordinem ostia]], etc.

paras.t: Quumque vidisset rex Esther reginam stantem, placuit oculis ejus. Erat enim pulcherrima, speciosissime quoque vestita, roseo colore vultu perfusa, gratis ac nitentibus oculis pollens, sicut infra legitur. Et extendit contra, id est versus, eam virgam auream pro signo clementiæ et amoris, quam tenebat in manu. Quæ accedens, osculata est summitatem virgæ, ad reverentiam regiæ dignitatis. Eratque virga illa sceptrum regis.
paras.en: [[5:2|And when he saw Esther the queen standing, she pleased his eyes|Quumque vidisset rex Esther reginam stantem, placuit oculis ejus]]. For she was most fair, and most beautifully clothed besides, [[Esth 15:8|with a rosy colour in her face|roseo colore vultu perfusa]], endowed [[Esth 15:8|with gracious and bright eyes|gratis ac nitentibus oculis]], as is read further on. [[5:2|and he held out toward her the golden sceptre|Et extendit contra, id est versus, eam virgam auream]] [*virga*, "rod", where the Douay-Rheims has "sceptre"], *toward* [*contra*], that is, in her direction, as a sign of clemency and love, [[5:2|which he held in his hand|quam tenebat in manu]]. [[5:2|and she drew near, and kissed the top of his sceptre|Quæ accedens, osculata est summitatem virgæ]], in reverence for the royal dignity. And that rod was the king's sceptre.

paras.t: Sed his contrariari videtur, quod infra legitur: Quumque elevasset rex faciem, et ardentibus oculis furorem pectoris indicasset, regina corruit, et in pallorem colore mutato, lassum super ancillam reclinavit caput. Josephus quoque: Rex (inquit) adspexit eam asperius, iracundoque vultu; et tunc apprehendit reginam membrorum debilitas, et super ancillas quæ prope latera ejus erant, repente collapsa est. Et simili modo Magister in historiis refert. Et respondendum, quod ea quæ in isto libro habentur ab eo loco, Dixitque Mardochæus, A Deo facta sunt ista, non habentur in Hebræo, ut dicit Hieronymus, et infra patebit, sed in editione vulgata sunt, et ex Josepho sumpta. Idcirco dicendum pro horum concordia, quod rex primo adspectu visa regina, fuit contra eam commotus, eo quod non vocata venisset: sed visa ejus discoloratione, verecundia, debilitatione, declinatione, rex subito fuit animo alteratus, et reginæ compassus, timens de morte ejus improvisa, prout hoc infra plenius enarratur: sicque regina, quum consolata fuisset et roborata ex verbis regis, osculata est virgam.
paras.en: But what is read further on seems to contradict this: [[Esth 15:10|And when he had lifted up his countenance|Quumque elevasset rex faciem]], [[Esth 15:10|and with burning eyes had shewn the wrath of his heart, the queen sunk down, and her colour turned pale, and she rested her weary head upon her handmaid|et ardentibus oculis furorem pectoris indicasset, regina corruit, et in pallorem colore mutato, lassum super ancillam reclinavit caput]]. Josephus also: The king, he says, looked upon her rather harshly and with an angry countenance; and then a weakness of the limbs seized the queen, and she suddenly collapsed upon the handmaids who were at her sides. And the Master in the Histories [Peter Comestor, in the *Historia scholastica*] relates it in like manner. And the answer is that what is found in this book from the place [[Esth 10:4|Then Mardochai said: God hath done these things|Dixitque Mardochæus, A Deo facta sunt ista]] onward is not found in the Hebrew, as Jerome says and as will be plain further on, but is in the common edition [the Vulgate], and taken from Josephus. Therefore, to reconcile these things, it must be said that the king, at the first sight of the queen, was moved against her because she had come uncalled; but seeing her lose her colour, her shame, her weakness and her sinking down, the king was suddenly changed in mind and had compassion on the queen, fearing her sudden death, as is related more fully further on[[Esth 15:11||]] [the margin reads "Esther xv" and then, unclearly, "13 et seq."; the passage begins at 15:11]: and so the queen, when she had been comforted and strengthened by the king's words, kissed the rod.

paras.t: Dixitque ad eam rex: Quid vis, Esther regina? Quæ est petitio tua? Etiamsi dimidiam regni mei partem petieris, dabitur tibi a me. Quamvis enim fuit regina, regnum tamen pertinebat ad regem; nec sine regis scitu et voluntate regina potest urbem aut partem regni alienare, aut alteri dare.
paras.en: [[5:3|And the king said to her: What wilt thou, queen Esther? what is thy request?|Dixitque ad eam rex: Quid vis, Esther regina? Quæ est petitio tua?]] [[5:3|if thou shouldst even ask one half of the kingdom|Etiamsi dimidiam regni mei partem petieris]], [[5:3|it shall be given to thee|dabitur tibi]] by me. For although she was queen, the kingdom nevertheless belonged to the king; nor can a queen, without the king's knowledge and will, alienate a city or a part of the kingdom, or give it to another.

paras.t: At illa respondit: Si regi placet, obsecro ut venias ad me hodie, et Aman tecum, ad convivium quod paravi per ministrantes. Ideo regem invitavit, ut quum factus esset rex potu solito more hilarior, proponeret ei suam petitionem. Ipsum quoque Aman invitavit, quia in ejus præsentia voluit eum regi accusare, ut rex contra præsentem magis incitaretur. Aliqui vero dicunt, quod ideo, ut alii principes incitarentur odio et invidentia contra Aman, eo quod sic honoraretur præ ipsis, etiam a regina; sed hoc, ut apparet, fuisset culpabile, nec apparentiam videtur habere.
paras.en: [[5:4|But she answered: If it please the king, I beseech thee to come to me this day, and Aman with thee to the banquet which I have prepared|At illa respondit: Si regi placet, obsecro ut venias ad me hodie, et Aman tecum, ad convivium quod paravi]] through those who serve. She invited the king so that, when the king had been made merrier than usual by drink, as is the custom, she might lay her petition before him. She invited Aman himself also, because she wished to accuse him to the king in his presence, so that the king might be the more stirred up against him there before him. But some say she did it so that the other princes might be stirred to hatred and envy against Aman, because he was so honoured above them, even by the queen; but this, as it appears, would have been blameworthy, nor does it seem to have any likelihood.

paras.t: Venit itaque rex et Aman ad convivium reginæ; quæ tunc regem rogavit, ut die sequenti, ipse et Aman rursus ad suum venirent convivium. Quod sic Deo ordinante peractum est, ut interim cor regis magis afficeretur ad Mardochæum quam ad Aman, et ipse Aman sibi ipsi foveam in quam caderet, præpararet.
paras.en: [[5:5|So the king and Aman came to the banquet|Venit itaque rex et Aman ad convivium]] of the queen; who then asked the king that on the following day he and Aman should come again to her banquet. This was so brought about by God's ordering, that meanwhile the king's heart might be more drawn to Mardochai than to Aman, and that Aman himself might prepare for himself the pit into which he would fall[[Ps 7:16||]].

paras.t: Egressus est itaque Aman a præsentia regis ac reginæ, illa die lætus et alacer ex tanta sua prosperitate, ut æstimavit, in die bonorum non exsistens memor malorum, nec providus periculorum sibi evenire potentium. Propter quod non implevit quod scriptum est: Sapiens in omnibus metuit. Quumque vidisset Mardochæum, non solum non sibi assurrexisse, sed nec motum de loco, indignatus est valde, reputans se sic parvipendi ab illo: quod superbissimus ferre non potuit, sed vehementer iratus fuit. Ira namque est appetitus vindictæ propter parvipensionem irascenti illatam, secundum Philosophum.
paras.en: [[5:9|So Aman went out|Egressus est itaque Aman]] from the presence of the king and the queen [[5:9|that day joyful and merry|illa die lætus et alacer]] at his so great prosperity, as he reckoned it: in the day of good things not mindful of evils[[Ecclus 11:27||]], nor foreseeing the dangers that might befall him. Wherefore he did not fulfil what is written: [[Ecclus 18:27|A wise man will fear in every thing|Sapiens in omnibus metuit]] [the margin as read gives Ecclus. xvii, 31; the words are those of Ecclus 18:27]. [[5:9|And when he saw Mardochai|Quumque vidisset Mardochæum]], [[5:9|that he not only did not rise up to honour him|non solum non sibi assurrexisse]], [[5:9|but did not so much as move from the place|sed nec motum de loco]], [[5:9|he was exceedingly angry|indignatus est valde]], reckoning that he was thus made light of by him: which, being most proud, he could not bear, but was vehemently angered. For anger is the desire of vengeance for a slight done to the one who is angry, according to the Philosopher [Aristotle].

paras.t: Et dissimulata ira: quam per signa monstrare, inhonestum ac stultum est, juxta illud Ecclesiastæ, Ira in sinu stulti requiescit. Et iterum Salomon loquitur: Fatuus statim indicat iram suam; qui autem dissimulat injuriam, callidus est.
paras.en: [[5:10|But dissembling his anger|Et dissimulata ira]]: for to show it by signs is unseemly and foolish, according to that saying of Ecclesiastes: [[Eccles 7:10|anger resteth in the bosom of a fool|Ira in sinu stulti requiescit]]. And again Solomon says: [[Prov 12:16|A fool immediately sheweth his anger: but he that dissembleth injuries is wise.|Fatuus statim indicat iram suam; qui autem dissimulat injuriam, callidus est]]

paras.t: Reversus est in domum suam, et exposuit suis omnem suam prosperitatem, addens quod quamdiu videret Mardochæum Judæum sibi odiosissimum ante fores palatii, miserum se arbitraretur. Moxque de consilio amicorum et conjugis fecit erigi trabem, id est crucem seu patibulum quinquaginta cubitorum, quatenus procuraret a rege ipsum Mardochæum suspendi in eo, et sic lætus ad convivium iret. Nam passio iræ sicut a tristitia inchoatur, sic ultione illata, ad delectationem (secundum Philosophum) terminatur. Placuitque ei consilium tanquam suæ passioni atque invidiæ consonum, et jussit parari crucem excelsam.
paras.en: [[5:10|and returning into his house|Reversus est in domum suam]], he set out to his own all his prosperity, adding that so long as he saw Mardochai the Jew, most hateful to him, before the gates of the palace, he would count himself wretched. And soon, on the counsel of his friends and his wife, he had a beam set up, that is, a cross or gibbet of fifty cubits, so that he might procure from the king that Mardochai himself be hanged upon it, and so go joyful to the banquet. For the passion of anger, as it begins from sadness, so, when vengeance has been taken, ends (according to the Philosopher) in delight. [[5:14|The counsel pleased him|Placuitque ei consilium]], as being in keeping with his passion and his envy, [[5:14|and he commanded a high gibbet to be prepared|et jussit parari crucem excelsam]] [*crux*, "cross", here the gibbet].

paras.t: Circa hæc quæritur, anne peccaverit Mardochæus, nullum penitus exhibendo honorem huic Aman. Et videtur quod imo, quia hoc fuit contra regis præceptum, et habuit speciem mali; scandalizativum quoque exstitit aliorum, imo et inflammativum ipsius Aman ad persequendum Judæos. Insuper, Mardochæus licite poterat aliquam saltem reverentiam facere Aman, in assurgendo seu alio modo, absque derogatione honoris soli Deo exhibendi. Et secundum apostolica documenta, obediendum est dominis etiam dyscolis, et ducibus a rege missis, quamdiu non transcendunt limites suæ auctoritatis in præcipiendo.
paras.en: On these things it is asked whether Mardochai sinned by showing no honour at all to this Aman. And it seems that he did: because this was against the king's command, and had the appearance of evil; it was also a cause of scandal to others, nay, it even inflamed Aman himself to persecute the Jews. Moreover, Mardochai could lawfully have shown Aman at least some reverence, by rising up or in some other way, without taking from the honour to be shown to God alone. And according to the teaching of the Apostles, masters are to be obeyed, even the froward[[1 Pet 2:18||]][[Eph 6:5||]][[Tit 2:9||]], and governors sent by the king[[1 Pet 2:14||]], so long as they do not pass the bounds of their authority in what they command [the margin notes here are only partly legible: "I Petr. ii(?), … 18; Eph. vi(?); Tit. ii, 9"].

paras.t: Ad hæc posset quis dicere juxta præhabita, quod Mardochæus ita se habuit, quia Aman voluit adorari et honorari ut Deus, secundum quod Lyra ad hoc allegat glossam Hebraicam. Sed hoc Rabbi Paulus multipliciter reprobat. Non enim, ut apparet, voluit altius honorari, quam rex Assuerus, qui non voluit adorari ut Deus; et si voluit sibi usurpare honorem divinum, derogasset regio honori: quod ex timore Assueri ausus facere non fuisset. Hinc addit Rabbi Paulus, quod glossa illa non tenetur ut authentica ab Hebræis; et quod sint duæ Hebræorum opiniones, cur Mardochæus noluit flectere genua coram Aman: una dicentium, quod Aman gerebat ad collum suum idolum quoddam, ideo noluit eum adorare, ne adorare illud idolum videretur; alia, quia Deus præcepit filiis Israel in Deuteronomio, ne obliviscerentur injuriæ eis ab Amalecitis illatæ. Et quoniam Aman fuit de stirpe illorum, noluit signa amicitiæ aut reverentiæ ipsi Aman ostendere.
paras.en: To this someone might say, according to what was set down before, that Mardochai behaved so because Aman wished to be worshipped and honoured as God[[Esth 3:2||]], as Lyra alleges the Hebrew gloss to this effect. But Rabbi Paul [Paul of Burgos] refutes this in many ways. For, as it appears, Aman did not wish to be honoured more highly than king Assuerus, who did not wish to be worshipped as God; and if he had wished to usurp divine honour for himself, he would have taken from the king's honour: which, for fear of Assuerus, he would not have dared to do. Hence Rabbi Paul adds that that gloss is not held as authentic by the Hebrews; and that there are two opinions of the Hebrews as to why Mardochai would not bend his knees before Aman: one of those who say that Aman wore a certain idol at his neck, and therefore Mardochai would not worship him, lest he seem to worship that idol; the other, because God commanded the children of Israel in Deuteronomy not to forget the injury done them by the Amalecites[[Deut 25:17||]]. And since Aman was of their stock, he would not show signs of friendship or reverence to Aman.

paras.t: Verumtamen glossæ Hebraicæ consonat, quod infra Mardochæus in oratione loquitur Deo: Cuncta nosti et scis, quia non pro superbia fecerim hoc ut non adoraverim Aman superbissimum. Libenter enim pro salute Israel etiam vestigia pedum ejus deosculari paratus essem; sed timui ne honorem Dei mei transferrem ad hominem, et ne quemquam adorarem excepto Deo meo. Verum ad hoc Rabbi Paulus respondet, illud non haberi nec recipi ab Hebræis, qui de isto libro non habent nisi usque ad decimum capitulum inclusive.
paras.en: Yet what Mardochai says to God in his prayer further on agrees with the Hebrew gloss: [[Esth 13:12|Thou knowest all things, and thou knowest that it was not out of pride|Cuncta nosti et scis, quia non pro superbia]] [[Esth 13:12|that I refused to worship the proud Aman|fecerim hoc ut non adoraverim Aman superbissimum]]. [[Esth 13:13|For I would willingly and readily for the salvation of Israel have kissed even the steps of his feet|Libenter enim pro salute Israel etiam vestigia pedum ejus deosculari paratus essem]]; [[Esth 13:14|But I feared lest I should transfer the honour of my God to a man, and lest I should adore any one except my God|sed timui ne honorem Dei mei transferrem ad hominem, et ne quemquam adorarem excepto Deo meo]]. But to this Rabbi Paul answers that this passage is not found or received among the Hebrews, who have of this book only as far as the tenth chapter inclusive[[Esth 10:3||]] [the margin as read gives "Ibid. x, 5"; the Hebrew text ends at 10:3].

paras.t: Verumtamen mihi apparet, quod his non obstantibus, Mardochæus potuisset licite aliquem exhibere honorem Aman in assurgendo, vel simili modo, nec ex Deuteronomio illud fuit ei illicitum, quia Dominus jussit ne obliviscerentur filii Israel expugnare Amalecitas: quod jam fuit impletum per Saul et Samuelem. Propterea non videtur, qualiter Mardochæus excusetur de hoc, quod nullam voluit facere reverentiam impio Aman, nisi dicatur, quod ex occulto instinctu Spiritus Sancti se ita habuerit. Per quem modum plurima excusantur, quæ alias fuissent illicita: sicut quod Samson cum Philisthæis occidit se ipsum; et quædam feminæ sanctæ submerserunt se, ne a perfidis violarentur, prout libro de Civitate Dei Augustinus declarat. Hinc dicendum apparet, quod Deus qui voluit arrogantiam hujus Aman per Mardochæum et Esther dejicere, movit cor Mardochæi ad talem rigorem et irreverentiam circa Aman.
paras.en: Nevertheless it seems to me that, notwithstanding these things, Mardochai could lawfully have shown Aman some honour by rising up, or in some like way; nor was this unlawful for him by reason of Deuteronomy, because the Lord commanded that the children of Israel should not forget to fight against the Amalecites[[Deut 25:19||]]: which had already been fulfilled by Saul and Samuel[[1 Kings 15:1||]]. Therefore it is not clear how Mardochai is to be excused for refusing to show any reverence to the wicked Aman, unless it be said that he behaved so by a hidden prompting of the Holy Ghost. In this way very many things are excused which otherwise would have been unlawful: as that Samson slew himself together with the Philistines[[Judg 16:30||]] [the margin as read gives Judic. xv, 30], and that certain holy women drowned themselves lest they be violated by the faithless, as Augustine explains in the book of the City of God. Hence it appears that it must be said that God, who willed to cast down the arrogance of this Aman through Mardochai and Esther, moved Mardochai's heart to such severity and want of reverence towards Aman.

6.title: Declaratio capituli sexti: Noctem illam rex duxit insomnem
6.title_en: Explanation of the sixth chapter: That night the king passed without sleep

paras.t: Exaltatio Mardochæi hic describitur.
paras.en: Here the exaltation of Mardochai is described.

paras.t: Noctem illam, postquam rex et Aman comederunt primo cum Esther, rex duxit insomnem, Deo sic ordinante pro sublimatione Mardochæi. Unde Josephus ait: Deus malignam spem Aman deridebat. Nam regi somnum per illam abstulit noctem: qui rex nolens in otio vigilias perdere, sed ad gubernationem sui principatus eas habere, scribam jussit libros afferre. Hoc est quod subditur: Jussitque sibi afferri historias, id est libros historiales, et annales priorum temporum: quod supra expositum est. Quæ quum illo præsente legerentur, ventum est ad illum locum, ubi scriptum erat quomodo nuntiasset Mardochæus insidias eunuchorum, regem Assuerum jugulare, id est occidere, cupientium. Et quum scriba voluisset legendo procedere, detinuit eum rex, ut Josephus addit. Ait rex: Quid pro hac fide, id est fidelitate mihi a Mardochæo exhibita, honoris ac præmii consecutus est Mardochæus? Dixerunt ei servi ejus: Nihil omnino. His videtur obviare quod infra scriptum est: Præcepit ei, scilicet Mardochæo rex, ut in aula palatii moraretur, datis ei pro delatione muneribus. Ad quod poterit responderi, quod munera illa respectu beneficii tanti, tantoque regi exhibiti, modica erant, et quasi nullius momenti: ideo nil recepisse asseritur. Josephus tamen refert Assuerum interrogasse, an aliquid scriptum esset in libris qui legebantur de remuneratione Mardochæo facta. Responditque scriba: Nihil. Et tunc rex jussit scribam tacere, et interrogavit quæ sit hora noctis: et audiens quod dilucesceret, jussit ut sibi nuntiarent, quem amicorum ante aulam invenirent. Hoc est quod sequitur.
paras.en: [[6:1|That night|Noctem illam]], after the king and Aman had eaten for the first time with Esther[[Esth 5:5||]], [[6:1|the king passed without sleep|rex duxit insomnem]], God so ordaining for the exaltation of Mardochai. Hence Josephus says: God mocked the wicked hope of Aman; for he took away sleep from the king that night; and the king, not wishing to waste his waking hours in idleness, but to use them for the government of his realm, bade the scribe bring the books. This is what is added: [[6:1|and he commanded the histories|Jussitque sibi afferri historias]], that is, the books of history, [[6:1|and chronicles of former times to be brought him|et annales priorum temporum]]: which was explained above[[Esth 2:23||]]. [[6:1|And when they were reading them before him|Quæ quum illo præsente legerentur]], [[6:2|They came to that place where it was written, how Mardochai had discovered the treason|ventum est ad illum locum, ubi scriptum erat quomodo nuntiasset Mardochæus insidias]] [[6:2|the eunuchs, who sought to kill king Assuerus|eunuchorum, regem Assuerum jugulare cupientium]] [the print is damaged here; the words are read with the help of the Vulgate] (*jugulare*, that is, to kill). And when the scribe wished to read on, the king stopped him, as Josephus adds. [[6:3|he said|Ait rex]]: [[6:3|What honour and reward hath Mardochai received for this fidelity?|Quid pro hac fide honoris ac præmii Mardochæus consecutus est?]] (fidelity, that is, shown to me by Mardochai). [[6:3|His servants and ministers said to him|Dixerunt ei servi ejus]]: Nothing at all. What is written below seems to stand against this: [[Esth 12:5|And the king commanded him, to abide in the court of the palace, and gave him presents for the information|Præcepit ei, scilicet Mardochæo rex, ut in aula palatii moraretur, datis ei pro delatione muneribus]] [the margin, partly unreadable, gives Ibid. xii, 5]. To this it can be answered that those presents, compared with so great a benefit done to so great a king, were small and as it were of no account; therefore he is said to have received nothing. Josephus however relates that Assuerus asked whether anything was written in the books that were being read of a reward given to Mardochai; and the scribe answered: Nothing. And then the king bade the scribe be silent, and asked what hour of the night it was; and hearing that it was growing light, he bade them tell him which of his friends they found before the court. This is what follows.

paras.t: Statimque rex: Quis est, inquit, in atrio? Responderunt: Aman stat in atrio. Nam solito maturius venit, ut suggereret regi de suspendio Mardochæi. Verum, ut Salomon ait: Non est sapientia, non est prudentia, non est consilium contra Dominum, qui dissipat consilia malignorum, ne possint implere manus eorum quæ cœperant. Dixitque rex: Ingrediatur. Quumque esset ingressus, ait rex illi, scilicet ipsi Aman: Quid debet fieri viro, quem rex honorare desiderat honore præcipuo? Cogitans Aman, quod nullum alium rex, nisi se, vellet honorare: quia jam sæpe fuit expertus favorem regis ad se; et quia superbi reputant se honore prædignos, et frequenter æstimant se tales ac tantos ab aliis reputari, quales et quanti reputantur a se ipsis, quum longe sit aliter; respondit: Homo quem rex honorare cupit, debet indui vestibus regiis, et imponi super equum qui de sella regis est, id est quem rex solet equitare. Unde in Scholastica historia dicitur, Super equum regis. Josephus quoque narrat ipsum Aman dixisse: Induatur veste tua, quem honorare desideras. Et accipere regium diadema.
paras.en: [[6:4|And the king said immediately: Who is in the court?|Statimque rex: Quis est, inquit, in atrio?]] [[6:5|The servants answered: Aman standeth in the court|Responderunt: Aman stat in atrio]]. For he had come earlier than usual, to put it to the king that Mardochai should be hanged. But, as Solomon says: [[Prov 21:30|There is no wisdom, there is no prudence, there is no counsel against the Lord|Non est sapientia, non est prudentia, non est consilium contra Dominum]], [[Job 5:12|Who bringeth to nought the designs of the malignant, so that their hands cannot accomplish what they had begun|qui dissipat consilia malignorum, ne possint implere manus eorum quæ cœperant]] [the margin gives Prov. xxi, 30 and, misread, Job v, 12]. [[6:5|and the king said: Let him come in|Dixitque rex: Ingrediatur]]. [[6:6|And when he was come in, he said to him|Quumque esset ingressus, ait rex illi]], namely to Aman himself: [[6:6|What ought to be done to the man whom the king is desirous to honour?|Quid debet fieri viro, quem rex honorare desiderat]] with a special honour. [[6:6|But Aman thinking|Cogitans Aman]], [[6:6|that the king would honour no other but himself|quod nullum alium rex, nisi se, vellet honorare]], because he had often experienced the king's favour towards him already; and because the proud reckon themselves most worthy of honour, and often think that they are held by others to be such and so great as they are held by themselves, though it is far otherwise; [[6:7|Answered: The man whom the king desireth to honour|respondit: Homo quem rex honorare cupit]], [[6:8|Ought to be clothed with the king's apparel, and to be set upon the horse that the king rideth upon|debet indui vestibus regiis, et imponi super equum qui de sella regis est]], that is, which the king is wont to ride. Hence in the Scholastic History it is said: On the king's horse. Josephus too relates that Aman said: Let him whom thou desirest to honour be clothed with thy robe. [[6:8|and to have the royal crown|Et accipere regium diadema]].

paras.t: Ex hoc Lyra concludit, quod Aman aspiraverit ad regnum, sed Rabbi Paulus contradicit, et dicit non esse intelligendum, quod homo ille quem rex vellet honorare, accipiat regium diadema, sed quod equus ille qui de sella regis erat, esset de illis qui consueverunt regium diadema portare, quando rex equitavit in illis. Huic autem objectioni repugnat, quod subditur, super caput suum; sicque Magister in historiis refert. Quod autem Aman aspiravit ad regnum, apparentiam habet ex hoc, quod infra Assuerus rex protestatur: Qui, scilicet Aman, in tantum arrogantiæ tumorem sublatus est, ut regno nos privare niteretur et spiritu. Nam Mardochæum et Esther expetivit in mortem, ut illis interfectis, insidiaretur nostræ solitudini, et regnum Persarum transferret in Macedonas. Idem apparet ex eo, quod inferius denuo legitur, Aman voluit nocere Mardochæo pro duobus eunuchis regis qui fuerant interfecti. Et primus de regis principibus ac tyrannis, id est majoribus ac fortibus. Olim enim dicebatur tyrannus, rex, aut princeps fortis, a […], quod est fortis. Nunc vero vocatur τύραννος, violentus et irrationalis, qui sequitur voluntatem, non rationem. Teneat ejus equum.
paras.en: From this Lyra concludes that Aman aspired to the kingdom; but Rabbi Paul [Paul of Burgos] contradicts him, and says that it is not to be understood that the man whom the king wished to honour should receive the royal crown, but that the horse which the king rode was one of those that were wont to bear the royal crown when the king rode on them. But against this objection stands what is added: [[6:8|upon his head|super caput suum]]; and so the Master relates it in the Histories. That Aman aspired to the kingdom has likelihood from what King Assuerus declares below: [[Esth 16:12|But he was so far puffed up with arrogancy, as to go about to deprive us of our kingdom and life|in tantum arrogantiæ tumorem sublatus est, ut regno nos privare niteretur et spiritu]] (*he*, namely Aman). For [[Esth 16:13|he hath sought the destruction of Mardochai|Nam Mardochæum, cujus fide et beneficiis vivimus, et consortem regni nostri Esther cum omni gente sua, novis quibusdam atque inauditis machinis expetivit in mortem]] and of Esther, [[Esth 16:14|Thinking that after they were slain, he might work treason against us left alone without friends, and might transfer the kingdom of the Persians to the Macedonians|ut illis interfectis, insidiaretur nostræ solitudini, et regnum Persarum transferret in Macedonas]]. The same appears from what is read again further on: Aman [[Esth 12:6|sought to hurt Mardochai|voluit nocere Mardochæo]] … [[Esth 12:6|because of the two eunuchs of the king who were put to death|pro duobus eunuchis regis qui fuerant interfecti]]. [[6:9|And let the first of the king's princes and nobles|Et primus de regis principibus ac tyrannis]] [Denis's text has *regis*, the margin the Vulgate's *regiis*; *tyrannis*, “tyrants”, which he goes on to explain], that is, of the greater and stronger men. For in former times a king or a strong prince was called a tyrant, from […] [a word lost in the print], which means strong. But now one is called a *tyrannos* who is violent and irrational, who follows his will, not reason. [[6:9|hold his horse|Teneat ejus equum]].

paras.t: Dixitque rex: Fac, sicut dixisti, Mardochæo Judæo sumpta stola, id est regia veste, et equo. Dicunt aliqui, quod rex tacuit de regio diademate, quia non videbatur sibi competere, quod alter a rege uteretur diademate regio. Sed his obviare videtur, quod rex dixit ad Aman: Cave, ne quidquam de his quæ locutus es, prætermittas. Infra quoque habetur, quod Mardochæus egrediens de conspectu regis, coronam auream portavit in capite. Tulit itaque Aman stolam et equum, ad faciendum juxta regis præceptum. Et, sicut Josephus refert, quum invenisset Aman Mardochæum saccum indutum, et jussisset eum sacco exutum, circumdari purpura, Mardochæus putans sibi illudi, dixit ad Aman: Pessime omnium hominum, sic nostram calamitatem derides? Veritate autem cognita, acquievit.
paras.en: [[6:10|And the king said to him|Dixitque rex]]: [[6:10|and do as thou hast spoken|Fac, sicut dixisti]] [Denis's text has *sicut dixisti*; the margin gives the Vulgate's *ut locutus es*] [[6:10|to Mardochai the Jew|Mardochæo Judæo]], [[6:10|and take the robe|sumpta stola]], that is, the royal garment, [[6:10|and the horse|et equo]]. Some say that the king said nothing of the royal crown, because it did not seem fitting to him that anyone other than the king should use the royal crown. But against this seems to stand what the king said to Aman: [[6:10|Beware thou pass over any of those things which thou hast spoken|Cave, ne quidquam de his quæ locutus es, prætermittas]]. Below too it is said that Mardochai, going forth from the king's presence, [[Esth 8:15|wearing a golden crown on his head|coronam auream portavit in capite]] [the margin, partly unreadable, gives Esther viii, 15]. [[6:11|So Aman took the robe and the horse|Tulit itaque Aman stolam et equum]], to do according to the king's command. And, as Josephus relates, when Aman found Mardochai clad in sackcloth, and bade him put off the sackcloth and be clothed in purple, Mardochai, thinking he was being mocked, said to Aman: Thou worst of all men, dost thou so mock at our calamity? But when he learned the truth he consented.

paras.t: Expleto demum regis præcepto, Aman festinavit ire in domum suam, lugens et operto capite, ex confusione atque tristitia. Narravitque amicis et uxori. Cui responderunt sapientes, quos habebat in consilio, et uxori: Si de semine Judæorum est Mardochæus, ante quem cadere cœpisti, id est humiliari et dehonorari, non poteris resistere ei. Unde apparet, quod isti noverunt aliquid de libris et historiis Judæorum, quorum libri erant translati ad aliam linguam; vel ex Judæorum inter se commorantium relatione. Atque (ut dicunt Hebræi) legerunt, quod filii Israel comparantur stellis cœli et pulveri terræ, ut patet sæpe in Genesi et Deuteronomio. Ideoque dixerunt: Dum incipiunt cadere, prosternuntur et suppeditantur ut pulvis: dum vero incipiunt prævalere, exaltantur ut sidera. Hoc recitative commemoro.
paras.en: When at last the king's command had been carried out, [[6:12|and Aman made haste to go to his house, mourning and having his head covered|Aman festinavit ire in domum suam, lugens et operto capite]] [the print is damaged here; the words are read with the help of the Vulgate], out of confusion and sadness. [[6:13|And he told|Narravitque]] [[6:13|his friends|amicis]] and his wife. [[6:13|And the wise men whom he had in counsel, and his wife answered him|Cui responderunt sapientes, quos habebat in consilio, et uxori]] [Denis's text has *uxori*; the margin gives the Vulgate's *uxor ejus*]: [[6:13|If Mardochai be of the seed of the Jews, before whom thou hast begun to fall|Si de semine Judæorum est Mardochæus, ante quem cadere cœpisti]], that is, to be humbled and dishonoured, [[6:13|thou canst not resist him|non poteris resistere ei]]. From this it appears that these men knew something of the books and histories of the Jews, whose books had been translated into another tongue; or from the account of the Jews living among them. And (as the Hebrews say) they had read that the children of Israel are compared to the stars of heaven and to the dust of the earth, as is often plain in Genesis[[Gen 13:16||]][[Gen 15:5||]][[Gen 22:17||]][[Gen 28:14||]] and Deuteronomy[[Deut 1:10||]] [the margin, much of it unreadable, cites several chapters of Genesis, Numbers and Deuteronomy here]. And so they said: When they begin to fall, they are thrown down and trodden under foot like dust; but when they begin to prevail, they are exalted like the stars. I mention this as something reported.

7.title: Explanatio capituli septimi: Intravit itaque rex et Aman, ut biberent cum regina
7.title_en: Explanation of the seventh chapter: So the king and Aman went in, to drink with the queen

paras.t: Forma petitionis Esther reginæ hic ponitur.
paras.en: Here the form of queen Esther's petition is set down.

paras.t: Intravit itaque rex et Aman, ut biberent cum regina: imo ut etiam manducarent cum ea; sed per unum designatur utrumque, sicut et nomine comestionis communiter ipsa quoque potatio insinuatur.
paras.en: [[7:1|So the king and Aman went in, to drink with the queen|Intravit itaque rex et Aman, ut biberent cum regina]]: nay, that they might also eat with her; but both are signified by the one, just as by the name of eating, drinking too is commonly understood.

paras.t: Dixitque ei rex: Quæ est petitio tua, Esther? Respondit: Si inveni gratiam in oculis tuis, o rex, dona mihi animam meam pro qua rogo, id est, vitam meam conserva, atque a mortis laqueo eripe, et populum meum pro quo obsecro, id est, ad instantiam meam præserva a mortis periculo jam propinquo, nisi subvenias, populum de quo nata sum, et cujus membrum exsisto.
paras.en: [[7:2|And the king said to her|Dixitque ei rex]]: [[7:2|What is thy petition, Esther|Quæ est petitio tua, Esther]]? [[7:3|Then she answered|Respondit]]: [[7:3|If I have found favour in thy sight, O king|Si inveni gratiam in oculis tuis, o rex]], [[7:3|give me my life for which I ask|dona mihi animam meam pro qua rogo]], that is, preserve my life and snatch it from the snare of death, [[7:3|and my people for which I request|et populum meum pro quo obsecro]], that is, at my entreaty preserve from the peril of death, now near unless thou help, the people of which I was born and of which I am a member.

paras.t: Traditi enim sumus ego et populus meus, ut conteramur, jugulemur et pereamus. Atque utinam in servos et famulas venderemur, id est, venditio ista esset eligibilior, quam sic jugulari; esset tolerabile malum: quia tolerabilior est mors civilis, videlicet servitus, quam mors corporalis, et generalis etiam parvulorum ac feminarum: et gemens tacerem, id est, habendo patientiam, et sustinendo pro culpa mea, etiam mei ipsius dejectionem a regali excellentia ad statum ancillarem, quia invite propono querimoniam. Nunc autem hostis noster est, cujus crudelitas redundat in regem. Vir namque et uxor sunt una caro: ideo occisio uxoris redundat in virum. Esther autem fuit pars populi, quem Aman procuravit morti adjudicari. Dictum est quoque supra, quod Aman adspiravit ad regnum, et cogitavit mala in regem. Poterat item rex emolumenta pecuniarum et commoda consequi, ex Judæorum venditione, seu occupatione in servitiis regis, quemadmodum in Ægypto servierant Pharaoni: idcirco eorum occisio regi damnosa fuisset.
paras.en: [[7:4|For we are given up, I and my people, to be destroyed, to be slain, and to perish|Traditi enim sumus ego et populus meus, ut conteramur, jugulemur et pereamus]]. [[7:4|And would God we were sold for bondmen and bondwomen|Atque utinam in servos et famulas venderemur]], that is, would that such a sale were what is chosen, rather than to be slaughtered thus: [[7:4|the evil might be borne with|esset tolerabile malum]]; because civil death, that is, slavery, is more bearable than bodily death, and that a general one, even of little children and women: [[7:4|and I would have mourned in silence|et gemens tacerem]] [literally "and groaning I would be silent"], that is, having patience and bearing, for my sin, even my own casting down from royal excellence to the state of a handmaid; for it is against my will that I lay this complaint. [[7:4|but now we have an enemy, whose cruelty redoundeth upon the king|Nunc autem hostis noster est, cujus crudelitas redundat in regem]]. For man and wife are one flesh[[Gen 2:24||]]: therefore the slaying of the wife redounds upon the husband. Now Esther was part of the people[[Esth 2:7||]] which Aman procured to be sentenced to death[[Esth 3:8||]]. It was said above, too, that Aman aspired to the kingdom and devised evil against the king[[Esth 6:8||]] [the margin gives only "Esther vi"]. The king also could have gained profits of money and advantages from the sale of the Jews, or from their employment in the king's service, as they had served Pharao in Egypt[[Ex 1:11||]]: therefore their slaying would have been to the king's loss.

paras.t: Hostis et inimicus noster pessimus iste est Aman, qui adversatur vitæ nostræ ac regno. Quod ille audiens, illico obstupuit, id est, præ admiratione rei insuspicatæ, territus fuit valde, et quasi defecit, vultum regis ac reginæ ferre non sustinens, ex pavore et confusione.
paras.en: [[7:6|It is this Aman that is our adversary and most wicked enemy|Hostis et inimicus noster pessimus iste est Aman]], who is opposed to our life and to the kingdom. [[7:6|Aman hearing this was forthwith astonished|Quod ille audiens, illico obstupuit]], that is, in amazement at a thing unsuspected he was greatly terrified, and as it were fainted, [[7:6|not being able to bear the countenance of the king and of the queen|vultum regis ac reginæ ferre non sustinens]], from fear and confusion.

paras.t: Rex autem surrexit, et intravit in hortum arboribus consitum, id est ornatum et complantatum, pro refrigeratione iracundiæ suæ, et ne in impetu iræ ferret sententiam. Aman quoque surrexit, ut rogaret Esther pro anima, id est pro vita sua conservanda. Nam rege surgente, regina etiam surgens, ex debilitate, quam incurrit ex immoderata suæ teneritudinis alteratione, projecit se super lectum ad repausandum. Intellexit enim a rege sibi paratum malum, id est, ex dispositione et ira regis, consideravit sibi imminere periculum mortis. Ira enim non habet misericordiam, nec erumpens furor. Et impetum concitati spiritus sustinere quis poterit? Atque, ut iterum Salomon fassus est: Quemadmodum hilaritas regis est quasi ros super herbam, sic iracundia ejus est tanquam fremitus leonis, et nuntius mortis.
paras.en: [[7:7|But the king being angry rose up|Rex autem surrexit]], and went [[7:7|into the garden set with trees|et intravit in hortum arboribus consitum]], *set* [*consitum*], that is, adorned and planted all over, to cool his anger, and lest he should pass sentence in the heat of wrath. [[7:7|Aman also rose up to entreat Esther|Aman quoque surrexit, ut rogaret Esther]] [[7:7|for his life|pro anima]] [*anima*, literally "soul"], that is, for his life to be spared. For when the king rose, the queen also rose, and from the weakness which she had incurred through the excessive shock to her tender nature, threw herself upon the couch to rest. [[7:7|for he understood that evil was prepared for him by the king|Intellexit enim a rege sibi paratum malum]], that is, from the king's disposition and anger he saw that the peril of death hung over him. [[Prov 27:4|Anger hath no mercy: nor fury, when it breaketh forth: and who can bear the violence of one provoked?|Ira enim non habet misericordiam, nec erumpens furor. Et impetum concitati spiritus sustinere quis poterit?]] And, as Solomon again has declared: As the cheerfulness of a king is as the dew upon the grass, so his anger is like the roaring of a lion, and a messenger of death[[Prov 19:12||]][[Prov 16:14||]] [Denis joins Prov 19:12 and 16:14; the margin notes here are only partly legible].

paras.t: Qui rex reversus, reperit Aman super lectulum corruisse, in quo, id est super quem, jacebat Esther cum vestibus. Dicunt aliqui, quod Aman ex debilitatione corruit super lectum: quia ex tantis et tam inopinatis adversitatibus et obstupefactione ac formidine debilitabatur in corpore. Josephus vero ait, quod procidit super lectum, rogans reginam. Et ait rex ex suspicione: Etiam reginam vult opprimere me præsente, id est strangulare, ut quidam exponunt, vel violenter cognoscere. Unde Josephus narrat regem dixisse: Pessime omnium, uxori meæ violentiam inferre conaris? Et statim operuerunt faciem ejus tanquam protinus condemnandi, et jam quasi condemnati ad mortem. Sic enim in aliquibus terris, solent damnatis ad mortem oculi operiri.
paras.en: [[7:8|And when the king came back|Qui rex reversus]], [[7:8|he found Aman was fallen upon the bed on which|reperit Aman super lectulum corruisse, in quo]], that is, upon which, [[7:8|Esther lay|jacebat Esther]] in her clothes. Some say that Aman fell upon the couch from weakness, because he was weakened in body by such great and such unlooked-for adversities, and by stupor and dread. But Josephus says that he fell down upon the couch entreating the queen. [[7:8|and he said|Et ait rex]] out of suspicion: [[7:8|He will force the queen also in my presence|Etiam reginam vult opprimere me præsente]] [*opprimere*, "to overpower"], that is, strangle her, as some explain, or know her by violence. Whence Josephus relates that the king said: Wickedest of all men, dost thou try to do violence to my wife? [[7:8|and immediately they covered his face|Et statim operuerunt faciem ejus]], as one to be condemned forthwith, and already as it were condemned to death. For so in some lands the eyes of those condemned to death are commonly covered.

paras.t: Dixitque unus de eunuchis: En lignum, hoc est patibulum, quod paraverat Aman Mardochæo, stat in domo, id est infra septa domus ejus. Iste eunuchus fuit unus eorum qui iverunt pro Aman vocando ad mensam reginæ, et viderat illud patibulum, ac petivit, cui esset paratum; cui respondit unus servorum, quod Mardochæo: ut Josephus refert. Cui dixit rex: Suspendite eum in eo, id est ligno, per manus tortoris.
paras.en: And [[7:9|one of the eunuchs|unus de eunuchis]] said: [[7:9|Behold the gibbet|En lignum]] [*lignum*, literally "wood"], that is, the gallows, [[7:9|which he hath prepared for Mardochai|quod paraverat Aman Mardochæo]], [[7:9|standeth in Aman's house|stat in domo]], that is, within the precincts of his house. This eunuch was one of those who went to call Aman to the queen's table, and he had seen that gallows and asked for whom it was prepared; and one of the servants answered him, for Mardochai: as Josephus relates. [[7:9|And the king said to him: Hang him upon it|Cui dixit rex: Suspendite eum in eo]], that is, upon the wood, by the hands of the executioner.

paras.t: Suspensus est itaque Aman. In qua re patet fallacia prosperitatis mundanæ, incertitudo et instabilitas favoris humani, præsertim principum mundanorum; et qualiter Deus sanctus et justus, superbis resistat, qui mentem Assueri affecit, et vertit ad beneplacita sibi in isto negotio, quemadmodum scriptum est in Proverbiis: Cor regis in manu Dei est; quocumque voluerit, inclinabit illud. Estque impletum in Aman illud Ecclesiastici, Facienti nequissimum consilium, super ipsum devolvetur, et non cognoscet unde illi advenit illusio; et quod ait Psalmista, In laqueo isto quem absconderunt, comprehensus est pes eorum; illud quoque Proverbiorum, Qui fodit foveam incidet in eam, et qui volvit lapidem ad eum revertetur.
paras.en: [[7:10|So Aman was hanged|Suspensus est itaque Aman]]. In which is plain the deceitfulness of worldly prosperity, the uncertainty and instability of human favour, especially that of worldly princes; and how God, holy and just, resists the proud[[1 Pet 5:5||]], who moved the mind of Assuerus and turned it to his good pleasure in this business, as is written in Proverbs: [[Prov 21:1|the heart of the king is in the hand of the Lord: whithersoever he will, he shall turn it|Cor regis in manu Dei est; quocumque voluerit, inclinabit illud]]. And in Aman was fulfilled that saying of Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 27:30|A mischievous counsel shall be rolled back upon the author, and he shall not know from whence it cometh to him|Facienti nequissimum consilium, super ipsum devolvetur, et non cognoscet unde illi advenit]], namely the mockery [*illusio*][[Ecclus 27:31||]]; and what the Psalmist says: [[Ps 9:16|Their foot hath been taken in the very snare which they hid|In laqueo isto quem absconderunt, comprehensus est pes eorum]]; and that saying of Proverbs too: [[Prov 26:27|He that diggeth a pit, shall fall into it: and he that rolleth a stone, it shall return to him.|Qui fodit foveam incidet in eam, et qui volvit lapidem ad eum revertetur]]

paras.t: Hinc Josephus circa hæc scribit: Contigit mihi mirari in isto sapientiam Dei, quod non solum malitiam Aman punivit, sed quod excogitata ab eo contra alium tormenta, in ipsum convertit, et ceteros hoc sentire permisit, quoniam qui contra alium molestus fuerit, hæc in se primum cognoscat parata.
paras.en: Hence Josephus writes on these things: It has befallen me to marvel herein at the wisdom of God, that he not only punished the malice of Aman, but turned upon himself the torments he had devised against another, and let others learn this: that whoever does harm against another should know that the same is first prepared against himself.

8.title: Expositio capituli octavi: Die illo dedit rex Assuerus Esther reginæ
8.title_en: Exposition of the eighth chapter: On that day king Assuerus gave to queen Esther

paras.t: Liberatio Judæorum ad instantiam Esther facta hic recitatur.
paras.en: Here is related the deliverance of the Jews, brought about at Esther's entreaty.

paras.t: Die illo dedit rex Assuerus Esther reginæ domum Aman, cum facultatibus quibus ipse Aman privari promeruerat in se et in sobole sua, utpote reus criminis læsæ majestatis: et Mardochæus ingressus est ante faciem regis, tanquam amicus et successurus in loco, dignitate, principatuque Aman. Confessa enim est ei, scilicet regi, Esther, quod esset patruus suus.
paras.en: [[8:1|On that day king Assuerus gave the house of Aman, the Jews' enemy, to queen Esther|Die illo dedit rex Assuerus Esther reginæ domum Aman]], with the possessions of which Aman had deserved to be deprived, in himself and in his offspring, as guilty of the crime of treason [*læsa majestas*, injury to the sovereign's majesty]: [[8:1|and Mardochai came in before the king|et Mardochæus ingressus est ante faciem regis]], as a friend and as one to succeed to Aman's place, dignity and rule. [[8:1|For Esther had confessed to him|Confessa enim est ei]], that is, to the king, [[8:1|that he was her uncle|quod esset patruus suus]].

paras.t: Tulitque rex annulum, quem ab Aman recipi jusserat, et tradidit Mardochæo. Dederat quippe rex annulum suum Aman ad signandum: quem abstulit ei, dum eum a pristina dignitate deposuit, et contulit Mardochæo ad eosdem usus, ad quos datus fuerat ipsi Aman.
paras.en: [[8:2|And the king took the ring which he had commanded to be taken again from Aman, and gave it to Mardochai|Tulitque rex annulum, quem ab Aman recipi jusserat, et tradidit Mardochæo]]. For the king had given his ring to Aman for sealing; he took it from him when he deposed him from his former dignity, and bestowed it on Mardochai for the same uses for which it had been given to Aman.

paras.t: Esther autem procidit ad pedes regis, et locuta est: Obsecro, ut novis epistolis veteres litteræ Aman factæ de Judæorum occisione, corrigantur, id est, reprobentur et revocentur.
paras.en: But Esther [[8:3|fell down at the king's feet|procidit ad pedes regis]], and spoke: [[8:5|I beseech thee|Obsecro]], that by new letters the former letters of Aman, made concerning the slaughter of the Jews, [[8:5|may be reversed|corrigantur]], that is, condemned and revoked.

paras.t: Responditque rex Esther reginæ et Mardochæo: Scribite Judæis sicut vobis placet, ex regis nomine. Hanc auctoritatem rex dedit conjugi suæ et ejus patruo, quoniam de eorum justitia, prudentia, fidelitate fuit certificatus.
paras.en: [[8:7|And king Assuerus answered Esther the queen, and Mardochai|Responditque rex Esther reginæ et Mardochæo]]: [[8:8|Write ye therefore to the Jews, as it pleaseth you|Scribite Judæis sicut vobis placet]], [[8:8|in the king's name|ex regis nomine]]. The king gave this authority to his wife and her uncle because he had been assured of their justice, prudence and fidelity.

paras.t: Accitisque scribis et librariis regis, id est, dictatoribus atque scriptoribus epistolarum ac librorum vocatis, epistolæ sunt scriptæ ut Mardochæus voluerat, et missæ per veredarios, id est nuntios, qui secundum Josephum equites erant. Harum epistolarum formam ponit Josephus in hoc loco: quæ infra continetur.
paras.en: [[8:9|Then the king's scribes and secretaries were called for|Accitisque scribis et librariis regis]], that is, those who compose and those who write letters and books having been summoned, [[8:9|letters were written, as Mardochai had a mind|epistolæ sunt scriptæ ut Mardochæus voluerat]], [[8:10|and sent by posts|et missæ per veredarios]], that is, messengers, who according to Josephus were horsemen. Josephus sets down the form of these letters at this place; it is contained further on[[Esth 16:1||]].

paras.t: Quibus veredariis imperavit rex, ut convenirent, id est alloquerentur, Judæos per singulas civitates, et in unum præciperent congregari ipsos Judæos, ut starent pro animabus suis, id est pro defensione vitæ suæ, et omnes inimicos suos cum conjugibus et liberis et universis domibus, id est familiis seu cognatis, interficerent, inferendo illis, quod illi decreverant inferre ipsis Judæis. Et constituta est per omnes provincias una ultionis dies, id est tertiadecima mensis duodecimi nomine Adar: quo die jusserat Aman Judæos occidi. Sicque ordinante divina justitia, eo die prostraverunt Judæi adversarios suos, quo adversarii ipsos occidere decreverunt.
paras.en: [[8:11|And the king gave orders to them|Quibus veredariis imperavit rex]], [[8:11|to speak to the Jews in every city|ut convenirent, id est alloquerentur, Judæos per singulas civitates]] [*convenire*, "to meet" or "to address"], [[8:11|and to command them to gather themselves together|et in unum præciperent congregari]] (the Jews, that is), [[8:11|and to stand for their lives|ut starent pro animabus suis]], that is, for the defence of their life, and that [[8:11|all their enemies with their wives and children and all their houses|et omnes inimicos suos cum conjugibus et liberis et universis domibus]], that is, their households or kinsfolk, they should [[8:11|kill|interficerent]], bringing upon them what they had decreed to bring upon the Jews[[Esth 3:13||]]. [[8:12|And one day of revenge was appointed through all the provinces, to wit, the thirteenth of the twelfth month Adar|Et constituta est per omnes provincias una ultionis dies, id est tertiadecima mensis duodecimi nomine Adar]]: on which day Aman had commanded the Jews to be slain. And so, by the ordering of divine justice, the Jews laid low their adversaries on the very day on which their adversaries had decreed to kill them.

paras.t: Summaque epistolæ, id est tenor et sententia epistolarum prædictarum, summatim, id est breviter, fuit, quarum sententia infra diffuse habetur: paratos esse debere Judæos ad capiendam, imo et exercendam, vindictam de hostibus suis fautoribus Aman, cujus edictum exsequi intendebant. Denique epistolæ illæ materialiter erant multæ, sed una in forma et sensu fuit, hoc est una in specie.
paras.en: [[8:13|And this was the content of the letter|Summaque epistolæ]], that is, the tenor and purport of the aforesaid letters, in sum, that is, briefly (their purport is given at length further on[[Esth 16:1||]]): [[8:13|that the Jews were ready to be revenged of their enemies|paratos esse debere Judæos ad capiendam, imo et exercendam, vindictam de hostibus suis]] [Denis: "that the Jews must be ready to take, nay to execute, vengeance on their enemies"], the abettors of Aman, whose edict they meant to carry out. Now those letters were materially many, but in form and sense there was one, that is, one in kind.

paras.t: Egressique sunt veredarii celeres nuntios perferentes, id est, veloces ambasiatas secum portantes.
paras.en: [[8:14|So the swift posts went out carrying the messages|Egressique sunt veredarii celeres nuntios perferentes]], that is, bearing swift embassies with them [*ambasiatas*, embassies or messages].

paras.t: Mardochæus autem de palatio et de conspectu regis egrediens, fulgebat vestibus regiis, hyacinthinis, id est purpurei coloris, et aeriis, hoc est coloris aerii clari et albi, coronam auream portans in capite, amictus pallio serico atque purpureo. In tali apparatu, decore, et gloria fecit eum rex egredi, ut cunctis pateret auctoritas et potestas sibi commissa. Tamen aurea illa corona in pretiositate et forma a diademate regis distabat.
paras.en: [[8:15|And Mardochai going forth out of the palace, and from the king's presence, shone in royal apparel|Mardochæus autem de palatio et de conspectu regis egrediens, fulgebat vestibus regiis]], [[8:15|of violet|hyacinthinis]], that is, of purple colour, [[8:15|and sky colour|et aeriis]], that is, of the colour of the clear, white air, [[8:15|wearing a golden crown on his head|coronam auream portans in capite]], [[8:15|clothed with a cloak of silk and purple|amictus pallio serico atque purpureo]]. In such array, comeliness and glory the king made him go forth, that the authority and power committed to him might be plain to all. Yet that golden crown differed in costliness and form from the king's diadem.

paras.t: Omnisque civitas exsultavit, atque gavisa est, hoc est tota urbs Susa, nisi forsan paucis fautoribus Aman exceptis. Vel, Omnis, id est quælibet civitas regis, ad quam rumor horum devenit. Noverant enim superbiam Aman, et Mardochæi virtutem. Ideo de illius dejectione, et hujus promotione gloriabantur. In quibus verificatum est illud Proverbiorum: In multiplicatione justorum lætabitur vulgus; quum impii sumpserint principatum, gemet populus.
paras.en: [[8:15|And all the city rejoiced, and was glad|Omnisque civitas exsultavit, atque gavisa est]] [the margin gives the reading *lætata*, as in the Vulgate], that is, the whole city of Susa, except perhaps a few abettors of Aman. Or, *all*, that is, every city of the king to which the report of these things came. For they knew Aman's pride and Mardochai's virtue; therefore they gloried in the casting down of the one and the advancement of the other. In which was verified that saying of Proverbs: [[Prov 29:2|When just men increase, the people shall rejoice: when the wicked shall bear rule, the people shall mourn.|In multiplicatione justorum lætabitur vulgus; quum impii sumpserint principatum, gemet populus]]

paras.t: Judæis autem nova lux oriri visa est, id est copiosa materia jucunditatis et clarificatio oculorum. Ideo undique multipliciter lætabantur, in tantum, ut plures, id est multi gentilium et idololatrarum, eorum religioni et cerimoniis jungerentur, id est, ad Judaismum converterentur, colentes de cetero verum Deum per observantias cærimonialium præceptorum, imo et moralium et judicialium mandatorum, percipientes quod Deus Israel sic subvenisset populo suo, ejusque adversarios trucidasset tam inopinate atque celerrime. Grandis enim cunctos Assuero subjectos Judaici nominis terror invasit, ita quod nomine Judæorum audito, perterrebantur, quorum Deum credebant summum et omnipotentem.
paras.en: [[8:16|But to the Jews, a new light seemed to rise|Judæis autem nova lux oriri visa est]], that is, abundant matter of gladness and a brightening of the eyes. Therefore they rejoiced everywhere in many ways, [[8:17|Insomuch that many|in tantum, ut plures]], that is, many of the gentiles and idolaters, [[8:17|joined themselves to their worship and ceremonies|eorum religioni et cerimoniis jungerentur]], that is, were converted to Judaism, worshipping the true God thenceforth by the observances of the ceremonial precepts, and also of the moral and judicial commandments, perceiving that the God of Israel had so helped his people, and had slain his adversaries so unexpectedly and so swiftly. [[8:17|For a great dread of the name of the Jews had fallen upon all|Grandis enim cunctos Assuero subjectos Judaici nominis terror invasit]]: upon all, that is, who were subject to Assuerus; so that on hearing the name of the Jews they were terrified, for they believed their God to be supreme and almighty.

9.title: Declaratio capituli noni: Igitur duodecimi mensis, quem Adar vocari ante jam diximus, tertiadecima die
9.title_en: Explanation of the ninth chapter: So on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which as we have said above is called Adar

paras.t: Dies ultionis, quam Judæi in hostes suos exercuerunt, hic narratur, nec est difficultas in textu.
paras.en: Here is narrated the day of the vengeance which the Jews took on their enemies, and there is no difficulty in the text.

paras.t: Primo enim exprimitur tempus, quo ulti sunt suam injuriam in eos, qui concordaverunt, juxta voluntatem Aman, occidere ipsos Judæos et eorum diripere opes.
paras.en: For first is expressed the time at which they avenged their wrong on those who had agreed, according to Aman's will, to kill the Jews and plunder their wealth.

paras.t: Fama Mardochæi crescebat quotidie: quia virtuose et sapienter regebat, et res publica præ solito prosperabatur sub eo; et divulgabatur quod erat patruus reginæ, ipsumque regem sua fidelitate præservasset a morte: ideo principes et præfecti provinciarum, extollebant Judæos timore Mardochæi, quem principem esse palatii post regem, vel magistratum curiæ, et plurimum posse cognoverant, quia rex honoravit et habuit eum ut patrem.
paras.en: The fame of Mardochai [[9:4|increased daily|crescebat quotidie]]: because he ruled virtuously and wisely, and the commonwealth prospered under him more than usual; and it was spread abroad that he was the queen's uncle, and that by his fidelity he had preserved the king himself from death: therefore the princes and prefects of the provinces [[9:3|extolled the Jews for fear of Mardochai|extollebant Judæos timore Mardochæi]], [[9:4|For they knew him to be prince of the palace|quem principem esse palatii]] after the king, or chief magistrate of the court, [[9:4|and to have great power|et plurimum posse cognoverant]], because the king honoured him and held him as a father.

paras.t: Ita ut in Susis metropoli regni, quingentos viros Judæi occiderint, extra, id est præter et ultra, decem filios Aman. Quos quum occidissent, prædas de eorum substantiis tangere noluerunt, id est, nihil de possessionibus occisorum converterunt in proprium usum: quod fuit honestum, ne ex cupiditate, non æquitate, viderentur se vindicare.
