paras.en: [[9:6|Insomuch that even in Susan|Ita ut in Susis]], the capital of the kingdom, [[9:6|they killed five hundred men|quingentos viros Judæi occiderint]] [the margin gives the reading *interficerent*, as in the Vulgate], [[9:6|besides|extra]], that is, over and above, [[9:6|the ten sons of Aman|decem filios Aman]]. [[9:10|And when they had slain them, they would not touch the spoils of their goods|Quos quum occidissent, prædas de eorum substantiis tangere noluerunt]], that is, they turned nothing of the possessions of the slain to their own use: which was honourable, lest they should seem to avenge themselves out of greed and not out of equity.

paras.t: Qui, scilicet rex, dixit reginæ: Quid ultra postulas? Cui illa: Detur Judæis potestas, ut sicut hodie fecerunt, sic et cras faciant in Susis solum. In ipsa etenim urbe plures et potentiores fuerunt adversarii Judæorum, in qua et Aman personaliter habitavit. Ideo Esther rogavit ibi fieri ultionem per duos dies, et factum est ita.
paras.en: [[9:12|And he said to the queen|Qui, scilicet rex, dixit reginæ]] (he, that is, the king): [[9:12|What askest thou more|Quid ultra postulas]]? [[9:13|And she answered|Cui illa]]: [[9:13|let it be granted to the Jews|Detur Judæis potestas]], [[9:13|to do to morrow in Susan as they have done to day|ut sicut hodie fecerunt, sic et cras faciant in Susis]], in Susa only. For in that city the adversaries of the Jews were more numerous and more powerful, and there Aman had lived in person. Therefore Esther asked that the vengeance be taken there over two days, and so it was done.

paras.t: In ceteris vero urbibus percusserunt adversarios suos tertiadecima die mensis Adar, et quartadecima die cædere desierunt, ita quod illa die neminem occiderunt. Juxta quem sensum, in Susis cessaverunt percutere quintadecima die mensis Adar.
paras.en: But in the other cities they struck down their adversaries on the thirteenth day of the month Adar, [[9:17|and on the fourteenth day they left off|et quartadecima die cædere desierunt]], so that on that day they killed no one. In the same sense, in Susa they ceased from striking on the fifteenth day of the month Adar.

paras.t: Scripsit itaque Mardochæus omnia hæc in libro isto, cujus auctor est ipse, quamvis vocetur liber Esther, quia principalius tractat de ea, et ipsa principalior fuit in procuratione liberationis Judæorum; et litteris comprehensa, misit ad Judæos per totum Assueri imperium, ut quartamdecimam et quintamdecimam diem mensis Adar pro festis susciperent, id est, de cetero festivos haberent in memoriam beneficiorum Dei et victoriæ eis concessæ; quia in ipsis diebus se ulti sunt de inimicis suis, id est, quartadecima die mensis illius cessaverunt ab ultione Judæi extra Susa habitantes. Judæi autem in Susis habitantes, cessaverunt ab ultione quintadecima die: ideo voluit Mardochæus utrumque diem haberi solennem, ut vacarent epulis, sobrie tamen, et gaudio spirituali Deo regratiantes atque conviviis moderatis.
paras.en: [[9:20|And Mardochai wrote all these things|Scripsit itaque Mardochæus omnia hæc]] in this book, of which he himself is the author, though it is called the book of Esther, because it treats chiefly of her, and she had the chief part in procuring the deliverance of the Jews; [[9:20|and sent them comprised in letters to the Jews|et litteris comprehensa, misit ad Judæos]] throughout the whole empire of Assuerus, [[9:21|That they should receive the fourteenth and fifteenth day of the month Adar for holy days|ut quartamdecimam et quintamdecimam diem mensis Adar pro festis susciperent]], that is, keep them as feasts thenceforth in memory of the benefits of God and of the victory granted them; [[9:22|Because on those days the Jews revenged themselves of their enemies|quia in ipsis diebus se ulti sunt de inimicis suis]]: that is, on the fourteenth day of that month the Jews dwelling outside Susa ceased from vengeance, while the Jews dwelling in Susa ceased from vengeance on the fifteenth day. Therefore Mardochai wished both days to be kept solemn, that they might give themselves to feasting, though soberly, and to spiritual joy, giving thanks to God, and to moderate banquets.

paras.t: Consequenter ponitur recapitulatio prædictorum. Aman enim filius Amadathi, etc. Atque ex illo tempore institutionis solennitatis istius, dies isti festivi, scilicet quartusdecimus et quintusdecimus mensis Adar, appellati sunt a Mardochæo et sequacibus ejus, Phurim, id est sortium, eo quod Phur, id est sors, in urnam missa fuerit, non a Judæis, sed ab Aman, ut supra expositum est. Fuitque una sors in communi, sed duæ in particulari, ut tactum est ibi. Ideo hic dicitur, Dies sortium, in plurali; et additur, Eo quod sors, in singulari. Itaque dicti sunt dies Sortium, ab eventu, non proprie a materia; et quia sors illa fuit occasio ultionis seu victoriæ, de qua principaliter fuit ista celebritas. Verumtamen Josephus refert, quod Judæi vocant hos dies, conversatores, quia videlicet in eis de mœrore gravissimo in gaudium sunt conversi; vel quia tunc pariter conversantur in epulis et ferculorum mutuis transmissionibus ac donorum largitionibus.
paras.en: Next a recapitulation of what has been said is set down: [[9:24|For Aman, the son of Amadathi|Aman enim filius Amadathi]], etc. [[9:26|And since that time|Atque ex illo tempore]] of the institution of this solemnity, [[9:26|these days|dies isti]] of feast, namely the fourteenth and fifteenth of the month Adar, [[9:26|are called|appellati sunt]] by Mardochai and his followers [[9:26|Phurim, that is, of lots|Phurim, id est sortium]], [[9:26|because Phur, that is, the lot, was cast into the urn|eo quod Phur, id est sors, in urnam missa fuerit]]: not by the Jews but by Aman, as was explained above[[Esth 3:7||]]. And there was one lot in common, but two in particular, as was touched on there. Therefore it says here *days of lots*, in the plural, and adds *because … the lot*, in the singular. So they were called the days of Lots from what came of it, not properly from its matter; and because that lot was the occasion of the vengeance or victory, which this celebration chiefly honoured. Josephus, however, relates that the Jews call these days *conversatores* [Denis's Latin form; he explains it from *converti*, "to be turned", and *conversari*, "to keep company"], namely because on them they were turned from the heaviest grief to joy; or because they then keep company together at feasts, in sending dishes to one another and in giving of gifts.

paras.t: Susceperunt itaque Judæi super se, id est, concorditer obligaverunt se ad celebrandum hos dies. Consensus enim exigitur ad novæ legis seu jussionis robur, auctoritatem et ratificationem. Isti sunt dies, quos nulla unquam delebit oblivio, et cunctæ quæ in toto orbe sunt provinciæ celebrabunt, id est Judæi habitantes in cunctis provinciis mundi: quod per hyperbolen dictum est.
paras.en: [[9:27|the Jews took upon themselves|Susceperunt itaque Judæi super se]], that is, they bound themselves with one accord to celebrate these days. For consent is required for the strength, authority and ratification of a new law or command. [[9:28|These are the days which shall never be forgot|Isti sunt dies, quos nulla unquam delebit oblivio]], [[9:28|and which all provinces in the whole world shall celebrate|et cunctæ quæ in toto orbe sunt provinciæ celebrabunt]], that is, the Jews dwelling in all the provinces of the world: which is said by hyperbole.

paras.t: Scripseruntque Esther et Mardochæus etiam secundam epistolam, ut omni studio dies ista, id est solennitas duorum dierum istorum, sanciretur, id est firmiter servaretur, in posterum, durante cursu veteris Testamenti. Et miserunt epistolam istam secundam, ad omnes Judæos imperii Assueri, ut haberent pacem internam cum Deo, et pacem externam inter se invicem et cum gentilibus, inter quos versabantur, non se extollendo aut insolescendo, eo quod regina et princeps palatii essent de natione eorum, et susciperent veritatem, acquiescendo veritati, doctrinæ atque justitiæ; vel, ut quidam exponunt, accipiendo hunc librum inter libros canonicos sacræ Scripturæ.
paras.en: Esther and Mardochai [[9:29|wrote also a second epistle|Scripseruntque Esther et Mardochæus etiam secundam epistolam]], [[9:29|that with all diligence|ut omni studio]] [[9:29|this day|dies ista]], that is, the solemnity of these two days, [[9:29|should be established|sanciretur]], that is, kept firmly, [[9:29|for the time to come|in posterum]], while the course of the Old Testament lasted. [[9:30|And they sent to all the Jews|et miserunt ad omnes Judæos]] of the empire of Assuerus, [[9:30|that they should have peace|ut haberent pacem]], inward peace with God and outward peace among themselves and with the gentiles among whom they lived, not exalting themselves or growing insolent because the queen and the prince of the palace were of their nation, [[9:30|and receive truth|et susciperent veritatem]], by resting in truth, doctrine and justice; or, as some explain it, by receiving this book among the canonical books of holy Scripture.

paras.t: Observantes etiam jejunia atque clamores, id est memoriam jejuniorum et clamorosarum orationum, quibus postulaverunt auxilium Dei adversus pericula eis ab Aman parata, antequam prævaluerunt modo prætacto. Porro Rabbi Paulus dicit istud ab Hebræis ita exponi, quod Esther et Mardochæus ordinaverunt, ut Judæi ante solennitatem hanc Sortium, vacarent orationibus et jejuniis pro gratia devotionis, et ad recordationem quod Esther, Mardochæus et alii Judæi, orando et jejunando, clamaverunt ad Dominum pro causa prædicta.
paras.en: [[9:31|And observe|Observantes]] also [[9:31|fasts, and cries|jejunia atque clamores]], that is, the memory of the fasts and the loud prayers with which they begged God's help against the perils prepared for them by Aman, before they prevailed in the way just described. Rabbi Paul [Paul of Burgos], moreover, says that the Hebrews explain this thus: that Esther and Mardochai ordained that before this solemnity of Lots the Jews should give themselves to prayers and fasts, for the grace of devotion and in remembrance that Esther, Mardochai and the other Jews, praying and fasting, had cried to the Lord in the aforesaid cause.

paras.t: Susciperentque ut observarent omnia quæ libri hujus, qui vocatur Esther, historia continentur, id est, crederent et approbarent universa, quæ in libro hoc, qui intitulatur liber Esther, sunt scripta.
paras.en: And that they should undertake to observe [[9:32|all things which are contained in the history of this book, which is called Esther|omnia quæ libri hujus, qui vocatur Esther, historia continentur]], that is, believe and approve all that is written in this book, which is entitled the book of Esther.

10.title: Expositio capituli decimi: Rex vero Assuerus
10.title_en: Exposition of the tenth chapter: And king Assuerus

paras.t: Deus qui nullum bonum deserit irremuneratum, Assuero regi magnam contulit prosperitatem terrenam, pro pietate sua circa Israelitas, et pro justitia quam in adversarios eorum exercuit. An vero fuerit tandem ad verum Deum ab idololatria per Esther et Mardochæum conversus, nescitur: quamvis infra satis monstretur habuisse notitiam quamdam veri Dei et providentiæ ac judicii ejus, beneficiorum quoque ipsius.
paras.en: God, who leaves no good unrewarded, bestowed great earthly prosperity on king Assuerus for his kindness towards the Israelites and for the justice he executed upon their adversaries. Whether he was at last converted from idolatry to the true God through Esther and Mardochai is not known; though further on it is shown clearly enough that he had a certain knowledge of the true God, and of His providence and judgment, and of His benefits as well.

paras.t: Rex vero Assuerus omnem terram et cunctas maris insulas fecit tributarias, id est sub tributo sibi deservientes: quod per modum hyperbolici sermonis est intelligendum, ad insinuandum quod valde magnam terræ partem et plurimas insulas, non tamen simpliciter omnes, sibi subjecit, intelligendo per terram et insulas, habitatores earum.
paras.en: [[10:1|And king Assuerus made all the land, and all the islands of the sea tributary|Rex vero Assuerus omnem terram et cunctas maris insulas fecit tributarias]], that is, serving him under tribute. This is to be understood as a hyperbolic manner of speaking, to convey that he brought under himself a very great part of the earth and a great many islands, though not simply all of them; by the land and the islands their inhabitants are meant.

paras.t: Cujus fortitudo, qua inimicis rebellibusque prævaluit, et imperium super subjectos, et dignitas monarchica, atque sublimitas qua Mardochæum exaltavit, scripta sunt in libris Medorum atque Persarum, quorum specialiter hereditarius rex fuisse refertur: ideo illi gesta illius specialius ac diffusius habebant descripta; et quomodo Mardochæus secundus a rege, id est primus post regem in ordine principum, fuerit, et magnus apud Judæos auctoritate, sapientia, bonitate, quærens bona populo suo, quia sollicitus fuit pro communi populi sui bono, et loquens quæ ad pacem sui seminis pertinerent. Sicque Deus per eum consolabatur Judæos dispersos.
paras.en: [[10:2|And his strength|Cujus fortitudo]], by which he prevailed over enemies and rebels, [[10:2|and his empire|et imperium]] over his subjects, [[10:2|and the dignity|et dignitas]] of a monarch, [[10:2|and greatness wherewith he exalted Mardochai|atque sublimitas qua Mardochæum exaltavit]], [[10:2|are written in the books of the Medes, and of the Persians|scripta sunt in libris Medorum atque Persarum]], whose hereditary king in a special way he is said to have been; and so they had his deeds written down more particularly and at greater length. [[10:3|And how Mardochai|et quomodo Mardochæus]] [[10:3|was next after king|secundus a rege]], that is, the first after the king in the order of princes, [[10:3|and great among the Jews|et magnus apud Judæos]] in authority, wisdom and goodness, [[10:3|seeking the good of his people|quærens bona populo suo]], because he was solicitous for the common good of his people, [[10:3|and speaking those things which were for the welfare of his seed|et loquens quæ ad pacem sui seminis pertinerent]]. And so through him God comforted the scattered Jews.

paras.t: Hucusque, seu usque ad hæc verba inclusive, liber Esther in Hebræo habetur. Idcirco Hieronymus mox subjungit: Quæ habentur in Hebræo, plena fide expressi. Hæc autem quæ sequuntur, scripta reperi in editione vulgata, id est translatione inventa et publicata, cujus auctor ignoratur, quæ Græcorum lingua et litteris, id est sermone et libris, continentur; et interim, id est medio spatio, post finem libri istius hoc capitulum ferebatur, id est, pars hujus capituli exprimebatur, videlicet verba immediate sequentia, Dixitque Mardochæus; quod juxta nostram consuetudinem obelo, id est veru, prænotavimus, id est, ante hæc verba posuimus similitudinem veru seu virgulæ, ad innuendum quod ista sequentia non sunt authentica seu canonica, sed transfodiuntur, hoc est, ab Hebræis non recipiuntur, imo tanquam superflua abscinduntur a canone Scripturarum.
paras.en: Thus far, that is, up to and including these words, the book of Esther is found in the Hebrew. And so Jerome straightway adds: “What is found in the Hebrew I have rendered with full fidelity. But these things that follow I found written in the common edition” [*editio vulgata*: here the Greek text in common use, not the Latin Vulgate], that is, in a translation found and made public whose author is unknown, “which are contained in the tongue and letters of the Greeks”, that is, in their speech and books; “and meanwhile”, that is, in the space between, “this chapter was carried after the end of the book”, that is, a part of this chapter was set down, namely the words immediately following, [[10:4|Then Mardochai said|Dixitque Mardochæus]]; “which, according to our custom, we have marked beforehand with an obelus”, that is, with a spit: that is, before these words we have set the likeness of a spit or small rod, to signify that what follows is not authentic or canonical but is pierced through, that is, it is not received by the Hebrews, but is rather cut off from the canon of the Scriptures as superfluous [the obelus, a mark shaped like a spit (*veru*), was set against passages to be struck out, so it “pierces” them. Denis follows Jerome's judgment here; the Council of Trent (1546) defined these chapters as canonical Scripture].

paras.t: Dixitque Mardochæus, post ipsius Aman suspensionem et suam promotionem: A Deo facta sunt ista. Tunc namque intellexit visionem quam ante habuerat, per rerum eventum et evidentiam facti: idcirco non fuit propheta ex visione hujusmodi, quia intelligentia est opus in visione. Recordatus sum somnii quod videram, hæc eadem quæ jam gesta sunt significantis; nec eorum quidquam irritum fuit, id est, nihil horum quæ vidi in somnio illo, inane fuit aut cassum.
paras.en: [[10:4|Then Mardochai said|Dixitque Mardochæus]], after the hanging of Aman and his own promotion: [[10:4|God hath done these things|A Deo facta sunt ista]]. For then he understood the vision he had had before, through the outcome of events and the evidence of the deed; and so he was not a prophet by reason of a vision of this kind, because [[Dan 10:1|there is need of understanding in a vision|intelligentia est opus in visione]]. [[10:5|I remember a dream that I saw|Recordatus sum somnii quod videram]], [[10:5|which signified these same things|hæc eadem significantis]] that have now been done, [[10:5|and nothing thereof hath failed|nec eorum quidquam irritum fuit]]: that is, nothing of what I saw in that dream was empty or vain.

paras.t: Vidit autem in somno parvum fontem, qui paulatim videbatur crescere et augeri atque exuberare in fluvium, et converti in lucem et solem. Vidit quoque duos dracones et duas gentes. Et per fontem parvum significata est Esther, quæ crevit sapientia, virtute, auctoritate et fama, ita quod instar lucis ac solis lætificavit et clarificavit populum suum. Hoc est quod dicitur: Parvus fons qui crevit, in imaginaria visione, in fluvium, et in lucem solemque conversus est, et in aquas plurimas redundavit, Esther est, id est, ipsam Esther designat.
paras.en: Now in his sleep he saw a little fountain, which seemed to grow little by little, to increase and to overflow into a river, and to be turned into a light and into the sun. He saw also two dragons and two nations. And by the little fountain Esther was signified, who grew in wisdom, virtue, authority and renown, so that like a light and like the sun she gladdened and brightened her people. This is what is said: [[10:6|The little fountain which grew|Parvus fons qui crevit]] in the imaginary vision [that is, the vision formed in the imagination, as in a dream, as distinct from bodily sight and from purely intellectual vision] [[10:6|into a river, and was turned into a light, and into the sun|in fluvium, et in lucem solemque conversus est]], [[10:6|and abounded into many waters|et in aquas plurimas redundavit]], [[10:6|is Esther|Esther est]], that is, signifies Esther herself.

paras.t: Duo dracones, ego sum et Aman, per significationem et proprietatem, ita quod comparamur draconibus, non tamen conformiter: quoniam ille dicitur draco per potestatis suæ abusum et venenatam impietatem, aliorumque pestiferam infectionem; ego autem per potestatis valorem et caritatis fervorem. Draco enim est ignea fera. Sic Christus significatur per leonem ratione fortitudinis, et diabolus ratione ferocitatis.
paras.en: The [[10:7|two dragons|Duo dracones]] [[10:7|are I and Aman|ego sum et Aman]] by signification and by a likeness of property, in that we are compared to dragons, yet not in the same way: for he is called a dragon by reason of the abuse of his power, his venomous impiety and the pestilent infection of others; but I by reason of the strength of my power and the fervour of my charity. For the dragon is a fiery beast. So too Christ is signified by the lion by reason of his strength, and the devil by reason of his ferocity.

paras.t: Gentes quæ convenerant cum uno dracone, hi sunt qui conati sunt delere nomen Judæorum, puta fautores ipsius Aman, volentes vitam et memoriam Judæorum omnino exstinguere. Gens autem mea, Israel est, id est Israeliticus populus me sequens draconem, quæ clamavit ad Dominum, et salvum fecit Dominus populum suum ab insidiis Aman; et fecit signa magna atque portenta inter gentes, dejiciendo Aman cum suis, et nos humiles exaltando;
paras.en: [[10:8|The nations that were assembled|Gentes quæ convenerant]] with the one dragon [[10:8|are they that endeavoured to destroy the name of the Jews|hi sunt qui conati sunt delere nomen Judæorum]], namely the abettors of Aman, who wished to blot out altogether the life and the memory of the Jews. [[10:9|And my nation is Israel|Gens autem mea, Israel est]], that is, the Israelite people that follows me, the dragon, [[10:9|who cried to the Lord, and the Lord saved his people|quæ clamavit ad Dominum, et salvum fecit Dominus populum suum]] from the plots of Aman; [[10:9|and hath wrought great signs and wonders among the nations|et fecit signa magna atque portenta inter gentes]], by casting down Aman with his own, and exalting us who were lowly;

paras.t: et duas sortes esse præcepit, id est partes seu eventus vel distinctiones, unam populi Dei, videlicet Judæorum fidelium, et alteram cunctarum gentium, hoc est infidelium idololatrarum. Venitque utraque sors in statutum ex illo jam tempore coram Deo universis gentibus, id est, ex decreto divini judicii quælibet gens accepit suam mercedem, et salvata est una, quæ clamavit ad Dominum, ac perdita altera.
paras.en: [[10:10|And he commanded that there should be two lots|et duas sortes esse præcepit]], that is, portions, or outcomes, or divisions: [[10:10|one of the people of God|unam populi Dei]], namely of the faithful Jews, [[10:10|and the other of all the nations|et alteram cunctarum gentium]], that is, of the unbelieving idolaters. [[10:11|And both lots came to the day appointed already from that time before God to all nations|Venitque utraque sors in statutum ex illo jam tempore coram Deo universis gentibus]] [Denis's text lacks *diem*, “the day”]: that is, by the decree of the divine judgment each nation received its due reward, and the one which cried to the Lord was saved, and the other destroyed.

paras.t: Ideo subditur: Et recordatus est Dominus populi sui, id est, ostendit se memorem Judæorum, eos pie exaudiendo, ac misertus hereditatis suæ, hoc est hereditariæ plebis suæ: de qua ait per Isaiam, Hereditas mea Israel.
paras.en: Therefore it is added: [[10:12|And the Lord remembered his people|Et recordatus est Dominus populi sui]], that is, He showed Himself mindful of the Jews by graciously hearing them, [[10:12|and had mercy on his inheritance|ac misertus hereditatis suæ]], that is, on the people that is His inheritance, of whom He says by Isaias: [[Is 19:25|Israel is my inheritance|Hereditas mea Israel]].

11.title: Declaratio capituli undecimi: Anno quarto, regnantibus Ptolemæo et Cleopatra
11.title_en: Explanation of the eleventh chapter: In the fourth year of the reign of Ptolemy and Cleopatra

paras.t: Hoc capitulum undecimum modice differt a præcedenti, quia ejusdem somnii descriptio est.
paras.en: This eleventh chapter differs little from the preceding one, because it is a description of the same dream.

paras.t: Itaque, Anno quarto, regnantibus Ptolemæo rege Ægypti, et Cleopatra conjuge, attulerunt Dositheus et filius ejus hanc epistolam Phurim, id est sortium. Vidit somnium Mardochæus: quod præcedenti articulo expositum est, sed hic aliqua verba adduntur. Erat autem Mardochæus de eo numero captivorum, quos transtulerat Nabuchodonosor cum Jechonia rege Juda, prout supra expositum est. Et ex isto patet verum esse quod dictum est ibi, videlicet Mardochæum cum Jechonia fuisse captum.
paras.en: So: [[11:1|In the fourth year of the reign of Ptolemy|Anno quarto, regnantibus Ptolemæo]] king of Egypt, [[11:1|and Cleopatra|et Cleopatra]] his wife, Dositheus and his son [[11:1|brought this epistle of Phurim|attulerunt Dosithæus, qui se sacerdotem et Levitici generis ferebat, et Ptolemæus filius ejus, hanc epistolam phurim]], that is, of lots. [[11:3|had a dream|Vidit somnium]] Mardochai: which was explained in the preceding article[[Esth 10:5||]], but here some words are added. [[11:4|Now he was of the number of the captives, whom Nabuchodonosor|Erat autem Mardochæus de eo numero captivorum, quos transtulerat Nabuchodonosor]] [[11:4|with Jechonias king of Juda|cum Jechonia rege Juda]], as was explained above[[Esth 2:6||]]. And from this it is plain that what was said there is true, namely that Mardochai was taken captive with Jechonias.

paras.t: Et hoc ejus somnium fuit: Apparuerunt in somno imaginaria visione voces, id est clamores, et tumultus et tonitrua et terræ motus, et conturbatio magna super terram: per quæ omnia præfigurabatur tempestas, inquietudo et vehementia tribulationis imminentis populo Judæorum in regno Assueri sub tempore Mardochæi et Aman. Talia quoque apparuerunt non imaginarie tantum, sed vere realiter in nativitate Alexandri regis, ad præsignandum vehementiam tribulationum imminentium orientalibus regnis atque provinciis ab Alexandro tunc nato.
paras.en: [[11:5|And this was his dream|Et hoc ejus somnium fuit]]: there appeared in his sleep, in an imaginary vision [that is, one seen in images in the imagination], [[11:5|voices|voces]], that is, cries, [[11:5|and tumults, and thunders, and earthquakes|et tumultus et tonitrua et terræ motus]], [[11:5|and a disturbance upon the earth|et conturbatio magna super terram]], a great one: by all which was prefigured the storm, the unrest and the violence of the tribulation hanging over the people of the Jews in the kingdom of Assuerus, in the time of Mardochai and Aman. Such things also appeared, not in imagination only but truly and really, at the birth of king Alexander, to foreshow the violence of the tribulations that hung over the eastern kingdoms and provinces from Alexander, then born.

paras.t: Et ecce duo dracones magni, paratique contra se in prælium, scilicet Mardochæus et Aman, juxta præhabitam in præcedenti articulo expositionem; ad quorum clamorem contra se invicem, cunctæ concitatæ sunt nationes, id est quædam de omnibus, regni præsertim Assueri, adhærentes impio Aman, ut pugnarent contra gentem justorum, id est, Judæos veri Dei cultores occiderent. Fuitque dies illa, id est tempus designatum per somnium illud, tenebrarum, id est tristitiarum, et discriminis, id est periculi, tribulationis et angustiæ, et ingens formido super terram: et hoc primo in populo Judæorum, promulgato edicto de eorum occisione: postea autem in fautoribus Aman, misso decreto, quod a Judæis essent interimendi. Conturbataque est gens justorum, scilicet Judæorum, timentium mala sua, id est adversa eis instantia, prout dictum est jam plenius, et præparata ad mortem, id est tradita et exposita periculo mortis ex machinationibus Aman.
paras.en: [[11:6|And behold two great dragons|Et ecce duo dracones magni]] [[11:6|ready to fight one against another|paratique contra se in prælium]], namely Mardochai and Aman, according to the explanation given in the preceding article[[Esth 10:7||]]; [[11:7|And at their cry|ad quorum clamorem]] against each other [[11:7|all nations were stirred up|cunctæ concitatæ sunt nationes]], that is, some of all nations, especially of the kingdom of Assuerus, cleaving to the wicked Aman, [[11:7|to fight against the nation of the just|ut pugnarent contra gentem justorum]], that is, to kill the Jews, worshippers of the true God. [[11:8|And that was a day|Fuitque dies illa]], that is, the time signified by that dream, [[11:8|of darkness|tenebrarum]], that is, of sorrows, [[11:8|and danger|et discriminis]], that is, peril, [[11:8|of tribulation and distress, and great fear upon the earth|tribulationis et angustiæ, et ingens formido super terram]]: and this first among the people of the Jews, when the edict of their slaughter was published[[Esth 3:13||]], but afterwards among the abettors of Aman, when the decree was sent that they were to be slain by the Jews[[Esth 8:11||]]. [[11:9|And the nation of the just was troubled|Conturbataque est gens justorum]], namely of the Jews, [[11:9|fearing their own evils|timentium mala sua]], that is, the adversities pressing upon them, as has already been told more fully, [[11:9|and was prepared for death|et præparata ad mortem]], that is, delivered up and exposed to the peril of death by the machinations of Aman.

paras.t: Clamaveruntque ad Deum; et illis vociferantibus in oratione, fletu, et gemitu, fons parvus crevit in fluvium maximum, id est, humilis Esther, origo consolationis et gaudii Judæorum, exaltata est valde et exaudita a rege in tantum, quod toti populo suo impetravit abundantiam exhilarationis, pacis et prosperitatis. Hinc subditur: Lux et sol ortus est, id est, Esther surrexit, et jucunditatem ac clarificationem procuravit Judæis. Quod et de Mardochæi elevatione potest intelligi: quo exeunte de regis conspectu cum regiis vestibus, coronaque aurea, visa est Judæis lux nova oriri. Humiles exaltati sunt, scilicet Esther, Mardochæus et Judæi, qui ad Deum humiliter confugerunt, et devoraverunt inclytos: quia penitus superaverunt principem Aman, et filios ac fautores ipsius.
paras.en: [[11:10|And they cried to God|Clamaveruntque ad Deum]]: [[11:10|and as they were crying|et illis vociferantibus]] in prayer, weeping and groaning, [[11:10|a little fountain grew into a very great river|fons parvus crevit in fluvium maximum]], that is, the humble Esther, the source of the Jews' consolation and joy, was greatly exalted[[Esth 10:6||]], and heard by the king so far that she obtained for all her people an abundance of gladness, peace and prosperity. Hence it is added: [[11:11|The light and the sun rose up|Lux et sol ortus est]], that is, Esther arose, and procured gladness and brightness for the Jews. This can also be understood of the raising up of Mardochai: when he went out from the king's presence with royal garments and a golden crown[[Esth 8:15||]], [[Esth 8:16|to the Jews, a new light seemed to rise|visa est Judæis lux nova oriri]]. [[11:11|and the humble were exalted|Humiles exaltati sunt]], namely Esther, Mardochai and the Jews, who fled humbly to God, [[11:11|and they devoured the glorious|et devoraverunt inclytos]]: because they utterly overcame the prince Aman, and his sons and abettors.

paras.t: Quod quum vidisset Mardochæus in somno et visione imaginaria: quam tamen tunc non intellexit. Nam subditur, et surrexisset de strato, id est lecto suo, cogitabat quid Deus facere vellet; et fixum habebat in animo id quod vidit, tenens pro certo, quod futurorum esset præsagium, et ardua designaret: ideo fuit cupiens scire quid significaret somnium: quod Deus sibi ostendit diu antequam res designata evenit, quatenus ea impleta, Mardochæus certius nosceret id ex divina providentia contigisse.
paras.en: [[11:12|And when Mardochai had seen this|Quod quum vidisset Mardochæus]] in sleep and in an imaginary vision: which however he did not then understand. For it is added: [[11:12|and arose out of his bed|et surrexisset de strato]], that is, his couch, [[11:12|he was thinking what God would do|cogitabat quid Deus facere vellet]]; [[11:12|and he kept it fixed in his mind|et fixum habebat in animo]], what he had seen, holding for certain that it was a presage of things to come and signified things of weight: therefore he was [[11:12|desirous to know what the dream should signify|cupiens scire quid significaret somnium]]: which God showed him long before the thing signified came to pass, so that when it was fulfilled Mardochai might know the more surely that it had come about by divine providence.

12.title: Elucidatio capituli duodecimi: Morabatur autem eo tempore in aula regis
12.title_en: Explanation of the twelfth chapter: And he abode at that time in the king's court

paras.t: Consequenter in hoc duodecimo capitulo recitatur, qualiter Mardochæus significavit Assuero insidias eunuchorum, prout supra est conscriptum.
paras.en: Next, in this twelfth chapter, it is related how Mardochai made known to Assuerus the plot of the eunuchs, as was written above[[Esth 2:21||]].

paras.t: Morabatur autem Mardochæus eo tempore in aula regis, cum eunuchis regis qui janitores erant palatii, et in primo palatii limine præsidebant. Quumque intellexisset cogitationes eorum per signa et facta quædam exteriora, vel per verba alterius linguæ, quam illi putabant Mardochæum non intelligere, sicut supra patuit: ubi ex Josepho allegatum est, quod servus unius eunuchorum illorum, natione Judæus, revelavit id Mardochæo: cui ille non credens, caute personaliter consideravit et observavit conatus eorum. Secundum quod subditur: et curas diligentius pervidisset, didicit quod conarentur in regem Artaxerxem, id est Assuerum, manus mittere violentas ad occidendum. Et nuntiavit super eo regi, id est de hac re significavit Assuero veritatem per Esther reginam.
paras.en: [[12:1|And he abode at that time in the king's court|Morabatur autem Mardochæus eo tempore in aula regis]] with [[12:1|the king's eunuchs, who were porters of the palace|eunuchis regis qui janitores erant palatii]], and had charge of the first threshold of the palace. [[12:2|And when he understood their designs|Quumque intellexisset cogitationes eorum]] by certain outward signs and deeds, or by words in another tongue which they thought Mardochai did not understand, as appeared above[[Esth 2:22||]]: where it was alleged from Josephus that a servant of one of those eunuchs, a Jew by nation, revealed it to Mardochai, who, not believing him, warily considered and watched their attempts in person. According to which it is added: [[12:2|and had diligently searched into their projects|et curas diligentius pervidisset]], [[12:2|he learned that they went about|didicit quod conarentur]] [[12:2|to lay violent hands on king Artaxerxes|in regem Artaxerxem manus mittere]] (Artaxerxes, that is, Assuerus), to kill him. [[12:2|and he told the king thereof|Et nuntiavit super eo regi]], that is, he made known the truth of this matter to Assuerus through queen Esther.

paras.t: Rex autem quod gestum erat, scripsit in commentariis, id est, scribi fecit in libris memorialibus, in quibus continebantur res dignæ memoria; datis ei, scilicet Mardochæo, pro delatione, id est accusatione eunuchorum, muneribus: quod qualiter intelligendum sit, in expositione superiorum est expressum.
paras.en: [[12:4|But the king made a record of what was done|Rex autem quod gestum erat, scripsit in commentariis]], that is, had it written in the books of record, in which things worthy of memory were contained[[Esth 2:23||]]; [[12:5|and gave him presents for the information|datis ei pro delatione muneribus]], *him*, that is, Mardochai; *for the information*, that is, for the accusation of the eunuchs: how this is to be understood was set out in the exposition of the earlier chapters[[Esth 6:3||]] [the margin notes here are barely legible; the passages are probably Esther 2:23 and 6:3].

paras.t: Aman vero gloriosissimus, id est honoratissimus et famosissimus, erat coram rege Assuero, qui fecit eum talem ac tantum, videlicet summum post se: et voluit nocere Mardochæo et populo ejus, procurando eorum occisionem, pro duobus eunuchis. Supra dictum est, quod voluit eos occidere, quoniam Mardochæus non flectebat genua coram ipso Aman. Hic vero innuitur alia causa: quia videlicet Aman ægre tulit, quod Mardochæus accusavit eunuchos regi, et occasio fuit interfectionis illorum, qui erant amici Aman, atque (ut aliqui opinantur) cupiebant promotionem ipsius Aman in regem.
paras.en: [[12:6|But Aman|Aman vero]] [[12:6|was in great honour with the king|gloriosissimus coram rege]] [*gloriosissimus*, "most glorious"], that is, most honoured and most renowned, before king Assuerus, who made him such and so great, namely the highest after himself[[Esth 3:1||]]: [[12:6|and sought to hurt Mardochai and his people|et voluit nocere Mardochæo et populo ejus]], by procuring their slaughter, [[12:6|because of the two eunuchs|pro duobus eunuchis]]. It was said above that he wished to kill them because Mardochai would not bend his knees before Aman[[Esth 3:5||]]. But here another cause is hinted at: namely that Aman took it ill that Mardochai had accused the eunuchs to the king and been the occasion of their being put to death; for they were friends of Aman and (as some think) desired the promotion of Aman himself to the kingship.

13.title: Elucidatio capituli tertiidecimi: Rex maximus Artaxerxes
13.title_en: Explanation of the thirteenth chapter: Artaxerxes the great king

paras.t: Capitulum præsens includit epistolam, quam misit Aman ex nomine regis Assueri de occidendis Judæis, orationemque Mardochæi.
paras.en: The present chapter contains the letter that Aman sent in the name of king Assuerus for the slaying of the Jews, and the prayer of Mardochai.

paras.t: Epistolæ autem hoc exemplar fuit, et sumptum est istud ex Josepho, qui undecimo Antiquitatum libro hanc ponit epistolam quasi de verbo ad verbum, sicut habetur hic, et insertum ac additum fuit editioni seu translationi vulgatæ, cujus auctor nescitur. Rex maximus Artaxerxes, alio nomine Assuerus, pro tunc monarcha, ab India usque Æthiopiam, etc.
paras.en: [[13:1|And this was the copy of the letter|Epistolæ autem hoc exemplar fuit]]; and this was taken from Josephus, who in the eleventh book of the Antiquities gives this letter almost word for word as it stands here, and it was inserted into and added to the common edition or translation, whose author is unknown. [[13:1|Artaxerxes the great king|Rex maximus Artaxerxes]], by another name Assuerus, the monarch at that time, [[13:1|from India to Ethiopia|ab India usque Æthiopiam]], etc.

paras.t: Quum plurimis gentibus imperarem, et universum orbem meæ ditioni, id est imperio, subjugassem: quod per hyperbolen dictum esse, tactum est sæpius. Non enim occidentalibus et citramarinis præfuit regnis. Volui nequaquam magnitudine abuti potentiæ. Hoc enim esset tyrannicum, abuti potentia. Propter quod in Proverbiis inducitur: Leo rugiens, et ursus esuriens, princeps impius super populum pauperem. Itemque: Dux indigens prudentia, multos opprimet per calumniam. Istud pulchrum proœmium præmisit impius Aman ex nomine regis, ne Judæorum occisio crudelitati adscriberetur. Sed clementia et lenitate, id est mansuetudine, gubernare subjectos. Roboratur namque clementia thronus regis, et mansuetudo maxime condecet præsidentes, quoniam ira excæcat et obruit oculum mentis, quem oportet in præsidentibus esse perlimpidum et tranquillum ad efficaciter judicandum. Ut absque ullo timore inordinato, vitam silentio transigentes, id est quiete pertransientes, optata cunctis mortalibus pace fruerentur. Omnia enim naturaliter appetunt suo modo pacem. Nam et motus tendit ad quietem, et bella ordinantur ad pacem; et sicut gravia deorsum, levia vero sursum quiescunt, sic appetitus humanus quiescit in pace. Sic et Apostolus Timotheum affatur: Obsecro fieri orationes, ut quietam et tranquillam vitam agamus in omni pietate. Nihilominus quidam ex corruptione naturæ seu habitu vitioso vel suggestione iniqua ad inquietudinem inclinantur, Isaia dicente: Impii quasi mare fervens quod quiescere non potest.
paras.en: [[13:2|Whereas I reigned over many nations|Quum plurimis gentibus imperarem]], [[13:2|and had brought all the world under my dominion|et universum orbem meæ ditioni]], that is, under my empire: that this was said by hyperbole has been touched on more than once, for he did not rule over the western kingdoms and those on this side of the sea. [[13:2|I was not willing to abuse the greatness of my power|Volui nequaquam magnitudine abuti potentiæ]]: for that would be tyrannical, to abuse power. Wherefore in Proverbs it is set down: [[Prov 28:15|As a roaring lion, and a hungry bear, so is a wicked prince over the poor people.|Leo rugiens, et ursus esuriens, princeps impius super populum pauperem]] And again: [[Prov 28:16|A prince void of prudence shall oppress many by calumny|Dux indigens prudentia, multos opprimet per calumniam]]. This fair preamble the wicked Aman set first in the king's name, so that the slaying of the Jews should not be put down to cruelty. [[13:2|but to govern my subjects with clemency|sed clementia et lenitate gubernare subjectos]] and mildness, that is, gentleness. For [[Prov 20:28|his throne is strengthened by clemency|Roboratur namque clementia thronus regis]] [Denis has “the king's throne”], and gentleness above all becomes those who rule, since anger blinds and overwhelms the eye of the mind, which in rulers must be quite clear and calm if they are to judge effectively. [[13:2|without any terror|Ut absque ullo timore]] [the margin gives the reading *terrore*, “terror”, for *timore*, “fear”] that is inordinate, [[13:2|they might live quietly|vitam silentio transigentes]], that is, passing their life in quiet, [[13:2|and might enjoy peace, which is desired by all men|optata cunctis mortalibus pace fruerentur]]. For all things naturally desire peace in their own manner. For motion too tends to rest, and wars are ordered to peace; and as heavy things come to rest below and light things above, so human appetite comes to rest in peace. So also the Apostle says to Timothy: [[1 Tim 2:1|I desire|Obsecro]] that [[1 Tim 2:1|prayers|fieri orationes]] be made, [[1 Tim 2:2|that we may lead a quiet and a peaceable life in all piety|ut quietam et tranquillam vitam agamus in omni pietate]]. Nevertheless some, from the corruption of nature, or a vicious habit, or a wicked suggestion, are inclined to restlessness, as Isaias says: [[Is 57:20|the wicked are like the raging sea, which cannot rest|Impii quasi mare fervens quod quiescere non potest]].

paras.t: Quærente autem me a consiliariis meis, quomodo hoc posset impleri, unus qui sapientia et fide, id est fidelitate, ceteros præcellebat. Hoc Aman ex nomine regis scripsit de se ipso; quum tamen in vitiosis et passionatis non sit vera prudentia, quæ est virtus, neque sapientia salutaris, quamvis possit esse in eis versutia quædam et scholastica notitia ac informis cognitio. Indicavit mihi in toto orbe terrarum populum esse dispersum, etc. Quod quum didicissemus, videntes unam gentem rebellem adversus omne hominum genus, etc.
paras.en: [[13:3|But when I asked my counsellors how this might be accomplished|Quærente autem me a consiliariis meis, quomodo hoc posset impleri]], [[13:3|one that excelled the rest in wisdom and fidelity|unus qui sapientia et fide ceteros præcellebat]], that is, faithfulness. This Aman wrote of himself in the king's name; though in men who are vicious and ruled by passion there is no true prudence, which is a virtue, nor saving wisdom, though there may be in them a certain cunning, and school learning, and unformed knowledge [*informis*: “unformed”, that is, not given its form and life by charity]. [[13:4|Told me that there was a people scattered through the whole world|Indicavit mihi in toto orbe terrarum populum esse dispersum]], etc. [[13:5|Wherefore having learned this|Quod quum didicissemus]], [[13:5|and seeing one nation in opposition to all mankind|videntes unam gentem rebellem adversus omne hominum genus]], etc.

paras.t: Jussimus ut deleantur; quatenus nefarii, hoc est detestabiles et nominatione indigni homines, una die ad inferos descendentes quantum ad animas: quarum immortalitatem multi gentilium crediderunt seu cognoverunt; reddant, id est auferre desistant, imperio nostro, id est subditis nostro dominio ac nobis, pacem quam turbaverant.
paras.en: [[13:6|We have commanded|Jussimus]] that they [[13:6|shall be utterly destroyed|ut deleantur]]; [[13:7|That these wicked|quatenus nefarii]] [the margin gives the reading *ut*, as in the Vulgate, for *quatenus*], that is, detestable and unworthy to be named, [[13:7|men going down to hell in one day|homines, una die ad inferos descendentes]], as regards their souls, whose immortality many of the gentiles believed or knew, [[13:7|may restore|reddant]], that is, may cease to take away, [[13:7|to our empire|imperio nostro]], that is, to those subject to our dominion and to us, [[13:7|the peace which they had disturbed|pacem quam turbaverant]].

paras.t: Ecce sceleratissimus iste Aman quam apparenter dictavit istam epistolam, et suam coloravit ferocitatem atque invidiam. Quem in hoc multi usque in præsens sequuntur, qui sub specie boni et optimi mala et pessima tegunt, proponunt et practicant. Ideo simulatores et callidi, specialiter et enormiter provocant iram Dei; et illusores Deus illudet, corruentque fallaces in laqueum, quem aliis texunt.
paras.en: See how plausibly that most wicked Aman composed this letter, and gave colour to his ferocity and envy. In this many follow him even to the present, who under the appearance of what is good and best cover over, put forward and practise what is evil and worst. Therefore: [[Job 36:13|Dissemblers and crafty men|simulatores et callidi]], especially and enormously, [[Job 36:13|prove the wrath of God|provocant iram Dei]]; and God shall mock the mockers[[Prov 3:34||]], and the deceitful shall fall into the snare they weave for others[[Ps 9:16||]] [the margin's reference here is barely legible; probably Ps. ix, 16].

paras.t: Sequitur oratio Mardochæi. Mardochæus autem deprecatus est Dominum, post promulgationem epistolæ præscriptæ et decreti, memor omnium operum ejus, in generali, vel quorumdam de omnibus, seu operum naturæ et gratiæ ac gloriæ. Sicque ait Psalmista: Memor fui dierum antiquorum, meditatus sum in omnibus operibus tuis. Specialiter vero consideravit Mardochæus opera et beneficia Dei, Israelitis ab antiquis diebus exhibita.
paras.en: There follows the prayer of Mardochai. [[13:8|But Mardochai besought the Lord|Mardochæus autem deprecatus est Dominum]], after the publication of the letter and decree set out above, [[13:8|remembering all his works|memor omnium operum ejus]]: in general, or some of every kind, that is, the works of nature, of grace and of glory. And so the Psalmist says: [[Ps 142:5|I remembered the days of old, I meditated on all thy works|Memor fui dierum antiquorum, meditatus sum in omnibus operibus tuis]]. But in particular Mardochai considered the works and benefits of God shown to the Israelites from the days of old.

paras.t: Et dixit: Domine Deus, rex omnipotens. De quo loquitur Isaias: Dominus legifer noster, Dominus judex noster, Dominus rex noster. Cui dicit Jeremias: Non est similis tui, Domine; magnus es tu, et magnum nomen tuum in fortitudine. Quis non timebit te, o Rex gentium? In ditione tua, id est in tua potestate atque dominio cuncta sunt posita, quum sis universorum creator: cujus conceptioni, jussioni ac nutui necessario subest et paret omnis natura creata, jure creationis et auctoritate creantis; et non est qui possit resistere tuæ voluntati, qua vis aliquid absolute, ex volitione exsistente in te: quæ nunquam ab effectu sibi placito impeditur, sicut per Isaiam testatus es: Consilium meum stabit, et omnis voluntas mea fiet. Et rursus in Job dicit: Quis resistere potest vultui meo? omnia enim quæ sub cælo sunt, mea sunt. Si decreveris, id est deliberaveris, salvare Israel, id est Israeliticam plebem ab imminente periculo; nullus poterit impedire, et continuo liberabitur a te.
paras.en: [[13:9|And said: O Lord, Lord, almighty king|Et dixit: Domine Deus, rex omnipotens]] [Denis reads *Domine Deus*, “O Lord God”]. Of Him Isaias speaks: [[Is 33:22|the Lord is our lawgiver|Dominus legifer noster]], [[Is 33:22|the Lord is our judge|Dominus judex noster]], [[Is 33:22|the Lord is our king|Dominus rex noster]]. To Him Jeremias says: [[Jer 10:6|There is none like to thee, O Lord: thou art great, and great is thy name in might.|Non est similis tui, Domine; magnus es tu, et magnum nomen tuum in fortitudine]] [[Jer 10:7|Who shall not fear thee, O king of nations?|Quis non timebit te, o Rex gentium?]] [[13:9|all things are in thy power|in ditione enim tua cuncta sunt posita]], in thy power and dominion, since thou art the creator of all things, to whose design, command and nod every created nature is of necessity subject and obedient, by right of creation and by the authority of the Creator; [[13:9|and there is none that can resist thy will|et non est qui possit resistere tuæ voluntati]], by which thou willest anything absolutely [that is, God's will taken simply, which always comes to pass, as distinct from what He wills only on a condition or permits], by a volition existing in thee: which is never hindered from the effect that pleases it, as thou hast testified by Isaias: [[Is 46:10|My counsel shall stand, and all my will shall be done|Consilium meum stabit, et omnis voluntas mea fiet]]. And again in Job He says: [[Job 41:1|who can resist my countenance?|Quis resistere potest vultui meo?]] [[Job 41:2|All things that are under heaven are mine|omnia enim quæ sub cælo sunt, mea sunt]]. [[13:9|if thou determine|Si decreveris]], that is, resolve, [[13:9|to save Israel|salvare Israel]], that is, the Israelite people, from the danger that hangs over them, no one will be able to hinder it, and at once it will be delivered by thee.

paras.t: Tu fecisti cælum et terram, et quidquid cæli ambitu continetur. Dominus omnium es auctoritate et jure creationis, conservationis, gubernationis et finalis dispositionis: ideo cunctis inest obedientialis potentia ad obediendum tibi tam naturaliter quam supernaturaliter, nec limitatur tua potestas immensa ad naturalem cursum ac ordinem rerum.
paras.en: [[13:10|Thou hast made heaven and earth and all things that are under the cope of heaven.|Tu fecisti cælum et terram, et quidquid cæli ambitu continetur]] [[13:11|Thou art Lord of all|Dominus omnium es]] by the authority and right of creation, preservation, government and final ordering: therefore in all things there is an obediential potency to obey thee, as well naturally as supernaturally [*potentia obedientialis*: the capacity of every creature to be raised by God to what lies beyond its natural powers], and thy boundless power is not limited to the natural course and order of things.

paras.t: Cuncta nosti, et scis quia non pro, id est ex, superbia, vel pro obtinenda excellentia aliqua, et contumelia alicui inferenda, fecerim hoc, ut non adorarem Aman superbissimum, etc. Istud supra expositum est.
paras.en: [[13:12|Thou knowest all things|Cuncta nosti]], [[13:12|and thou knowest that it was not out of pride|et scis quia non pro, id est ex, superbia]], or to gain some eminence, and to put an insult on anyone, [[13:12|that I refused to worship the proud Aman|ut non adorarem Aman superbissimum]], etc. This has been explained above[[Esth 3:2||]] [the margin's reference is partly misread; Esther iii, where Mardochai will not worship Aman].

paras.t: Et nunc, Domine, Deus Abraham, miserere populi tui, quia volunt nos inimici nostri, scilicet Aman et sui, perdere, et hereditatem tuam delere. Ne despicias partem tuam, id est Israeliticam plebem, quæ est parva in hominum universitate; quam plebem ad tuum cultum præ ceteris gentibus elegisti, redemisti ex Ægypto in patribus suis sub Moyse. Vel, Quam, cujus patres sic redemisti. Interdum enim loquitur Scriptura de pluribus seu diversis, quasi de uno aut eisdem.
paras.en: [[13:15|And now, O Lord|Et nunc, Domine]], [[13:15|O God of Abraham|Deus Abraham]], [[13:15|have mercy on thy people|miserere populi tui]], [[13:15|because our enemies resolve|quia volunt nos inimici nostri]], namely Aman and his, [[13:15|to destroy us, and extinguish thy inheritance|perdere, et hereditatem tuam delere]]. [[13:16|Despise not thy portion|Ne despicias partem tuam]], that is, the Israelite people, which is small among the whole of mankind; the people whom thou hast chosen for thy worship above the other nations[[Deut 14:2||]] [the margin's numeral is damaged; Deut 14:2 and 7:6 both say this], [[13:16|which thou hast redeemed for thyself out of Egypt|redemisti ex Ægypto]][[Ex 12:51||]] [the margin gives Exod. xii, its verse unreadable] in their fathers under Moses. Or, *which* means: whose fathers thou hast so redeemed. For Scripture sometimes speaks of many or different persons as if of one or the same.

paras.t: Exaudi deprecationem meam, et propitius esto sorti et funiculo tuo, id est populo tibi sequestrato ac partito: sicut per sortem venit alicui pars de toto; quod tamen ex tua providentia, non fortuitu, factum est ita. Et converte luctum nostrum in gaudium, eripiendo nos de imminente adversitate, ut viventes vita naturæ et gratiæ, laudemus nomen tuum nominatum, id est te ipsum, Domine, gratias referendo; et ne claudas ora te canentium, id est, ora nostra te laudantia in hymnis et psalmis, in lege et Prophetis, non permittas claudi per mortem violentam nobis certissime imminentem, nisi tu pie succurras.
paras.en: [[13:17|Hear my supplication|Exaudi deprecationem meam]], [[13:17|and be merciful to thy lot and inheritance|et propitius esto sorti et funiculo tuo]] [*funiculus*, “a cord”, the measuring line by which land was portioned out, hence a share], that is, to the people set apart and allotted to thee, as by lot a part of the whole falls to someone; yet this came about so by thy providence, not by chance. [[13:17|and turn our mourning into joy|Et converte luctum nostrum in gaudium]], by snatching us from the adversity that threatens us, [[13:17|that we may live|ut viventes]] the life of nature and of grace, [[13:17|and praise thy name|laudemus nomen tuum]], the one named, that is, thyself, [[13:17|O Lord|Domine]], by giving thanks; [[13:17|and shut not the mouths of them that sing to thee|et ne claudas ora te canentium]]: that is, do not let our mouths that praise thee in hymns and psalms, in the Law and the Prophets, be shut by the violent death that most surely hangs over us unless thou mercifully come to our help.

14.title: Expositio capituli quartidecimi: Esther quoque regina confugit ad Dominum
14.title_en: Exposition of the fourteenth chapter: Queen Esther also had recourse to the Lord

paras.t: Forma orationis Esther reginæ hic ponitur.
paras.en: Here the form of queen Esther's prayer is set down.

paras.t: Esther quoque regina confugit ad Dominum, id est, ad implorandum misericordiam subventionemque Dei se convertit. Itaque mentis conversione, non loci mutatione, ad Deum incircumscriptum ubique præsentem confugitur. Et pro unguentis variis, quibus aliquando utebatur, non ex carnali affectu, sed necessitate, ne regem offenderet, cui propter commune bonum populi sui placere habebat, cinere et stercore implevit caput, et corpus suum humiliavit jejuniis, id est, capiti suo superjecit cinerem, et corpus suum prostravit in terram, nec ab immunditiis illud more solito lavit: et forsan luto aut alia vili materia illud linivit, pro majore sui humiliatione, ad impetrandum auxilium pietatis divinæ. Omniaque loca in quibus ante lætari consueverat. Infra habetur in fine hujus capituli, quod non sit lætata in palatio regis, nisi in Deo Israel. Ideo sensus est: Omnia loca in quibus ante lætari consueverat, id est signa alicujus lætitiæ demonstrare, seu per modum lætantis forinsecus se habere. Potest quoque exponi de spirituali jucunditate, quam in actibus habuit virtuosis: sed hac vice intenta fuit doloribus. Crinium laceratione complevit, præ dolore extrahendo pro parte capillos capitis sui, quemadmodum et Esdras vel Nehemias se fecisse testatur. Complevit autem sic loca illa, id est, præ solito occupavit, ut sit hyperbolicus sermo.
paras.en: Queen Esther also [[14:1|had recourse to the Lord|Esther quoque regina confugit ad Dominum]], that is, turned herself to implore God's mercy and help. And so one has recourse to God, who is uncircumscribed and everywhere present, by turning of the mind, not by change of place. [[14:2|instead of divers precious ointments|Et pro unguentis variis]], which she used at times, not from carnal affection but of necessity, lest she should offend the king, whom she had to please for the common good of her people, [[14:2|she covered her head with ashes and dung, and she humbled her body with fasts|cinere et stercore implevit caput, et corpus suum humiliavit jejuniis]]: that is, she cast ashes on her head and laid her body prostrate on the ground, nor washed it of its uncleanness as she was wont; and perhaps she smeared it with mud or some other vile matter, for her greater humbling, to obtain the help of God's mercy. [[14:2|and all the places in which before she was accustomed to rejoice|Omniaque loca in quibus ante lætari consueverat]]. Further on, at the end of this chapter, it is said that she did not rejoice in the king's palace except in the God of Israel[[14:18||]]. So the sense is: all the places in which before she was accustomed to rejoice, that is, to show signs of some gladness, or outwardly to bear herself as one rejoicing. It can also be explained of the spiritual gladness which she had in virtuous acts; but this time she was intent on sorrows. [[14:2|she filled with her torn hair|Crinium laceratione complevit]], in her grief pulling out part of the hair of her head, as Esdras, or Nehemias, testifies that he did[[1 Esd 9:3||]]. And she so *filled* those places, that is, occupied them more than usual, so that the expression is hyperbolic.

paras.t: Et deprecabatur Dominum Deum Israel, dicens: Domine mi, per specialem devotionem mei ad te, et per gratiosam providentiam tui ad me, qui rex noster es solus, quia pro nunc non habemus proprium regem terrenum. Et tu solus rex noster es, per spiritualem gubernationem, regendo nos intus per fidem et gratiam ac directionem internam. Unde ait Psalmista: Deus autem rex noster ante sæcula; et: Dominus regit me, et nihil mihi deerit. Adjuva me solitariam, id est humana consortia evitantem, et tibi quantum mihi possibile est in secreto vacantem, atque eorum de quibus nata sum, societate privatam; et cujus præter te nullus auxiliator est alius, id est, in isto periculo nullus mihi potest efficax adjutorium præbere, nisi tu per modum tibi placentem.
paras.en: [[14:3|And she prayed to the Lord the God of Israel, saying|Et deprecabatur Dominum Deum Israel, dicens]]: [[14:3|O my Lord|Domine mi]], *my* by my special devotion to thee and by thy gracious providence towards me, [[14:3|who alone art our king|qui rex noster es solus]], because for the present we have no earthly king of our own. And thou alone art our king by spiritual government, ruling us within by faith and grace and inward direction. Whence the Psalmist says: [[Ps 73:12|But God is our king before ages|Deus autem rex noster ante sæcula]]; and: [[Ps 22:1|The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing|Dominus regit me, et nihil mihi deerit]]. [[14:3|help me a desolate woman|Adjuva me solitariam]], that is, one who shuns human company, and gives herself to thee in secret as far as she can, and is deprived of the company of those of whom she was born; [[14:3|and who have no other helper but thee|et cujus præter te nullus auxiliator est alius]], that is, in this peril no one can give me effective help but thou, in the way that pleases thee.

paras.t: Periculum meum in manibus meis est, id est, de proximo imminet, et quasi tam præsens et certum, sicut id quod manu tenetur, nisi tu aliter ordines.
paras.en: [[14:4|My danger is in my hands|Periculum meum in manibus meis est]], that is, it is close at hand, and as present and certain as what is held in the hand, unless thou order otherwise.

paras.t: Audivi a patre meo, quod tu, Domine, tulisses Israel de cunctis gentibus, id est, a ceteris nationibus separasti Israeliticum populum, mancipando eum tuo obsequio: juxta illud Deuteronomii, Te elegit Dominus, ut sis ei populus peculiaris de cunctis populis qui sunt super terram; et patres nostros ex omnibus retro majoribus suis, id est, Patriarchas Abraham, Isaac, Jacob applicuisti tibi, relictis prædecessoribus progenitoribusque eorum qui idolis servierunt. Hinc scriptum est in Deuteronomio: Patribus tuis conglutinatus est Dominus, et elegit eos. Josue quoque in fine libri sui ait: Trans fluvium (inquit) habitaverunt patres vestri, Thare pater Abraham et Nachor, servieruntque diis alienis. Ut possideres hæreditatem sempiternam, id est, quatenus Israeliticum populum haberes tibi jugiter servientem, et a te gratiose possessum: sicut in Deuteronomio legitur sæpe.
paras.en: [[14:5|I have heard of my father that thou, O Lord, didst take Israel from among all nations|Audivi a patre meo, quod tu, Domine, tulisses Israel de cunctis gentibus]], that is, thou didst set apart the people of Israel from the other nations, binding it to thy service: according to that saying of Deuteronomy: The Lord [[Deut 7:6|hath chosen thee, to be his peculiar people of all peoples that are upon the earth|Te elegit Dominus, ut sis ei populus peculiaris de cunctis populis qui sunt super terram]]; [[14:5|and our fathers from all their predecessors|et patres nostros ex omnibus retro majoribus suis]], that is, thou didst join to thyself the Patriarchs Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, leaving aside their predecessors and forefathers, who served idols. Hence it is written in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 10:15|the Lord hath been closely joined to thy fathers|Patribus tuis conglutinatus est Dominus]], and chose them. Josue too says at the end of his book: [[Jos 24:2|on the other side of the river|Trans fluvium]] (he says) [[Jos 24:2|Your fathers dwelt|habitaverunt patres vestri]], [[Jos 24:2|Thare the father of Abraham, and Nachor: and they served strange gods|Thare pater Abraham et Nachor, servieruntque diis alienis]]. [[14:5|to possess them as an everlasting inheritance|Ut possideres hæreditatem sempiternam]], that is, that thou mightest have the people of Israel serving thee continually and possessed by thee in grace: as is often read in Deuteronomy[[Deut 4:20||]][[Deut 14:2||]][[Deut 26:18||]][[Deut 32:9||]].

paras.t: Peccavimus in conspectu tuo. Hoc Esther loquitur in persona populi sui, connumerando se transgressoribus ex humilitate, quia fuit membrum plebis illius. Et simili modo loquitur Esdras: Peccata nostra creverunt usque ad cælum. Et idcirco tradidisti nos in manus inimicorum nostrorum. Coluimus enim deos eorum, puta gentilium, quibus nos tradidisti captivos: quoniam multi ex filiis Israel fuerunt idololatræ quando ab Assyriis et Chaldæis capti fuerunt, et ante frequenter temporibus Judicum.
paras.en: [[14:6|We have sinned in thy sight|Peccavimus in conspectu tuo]]. Esther says this in the person of her people, numbering herself with the transgressors out of humility, because she was a member of that people. And in like manner Esdras says: [[1 Esd 9:6|our sins are grown up even unto heaven|Peccata nostra creverunt usque ad cælum]]. [[14:6|and therefore thou hast delivered us into the hands of our enemies|Et idcirco tradidisti nos in manus inimicorum nostrorum]]. [[14:7|For we have worshipped their gods|Coluimus enim deos eorum]], the gods, that is, of the gentiles, to whom thou didst deliver us captive: for many of the children of Israel were idolaters when they were taken captive by the Assyrians[[4 Kings 17:7||]] and the Chaldeans, and often before, in the times of the Judges[[Judg 2:11||]] [the margin notes here are partly illegible].

paras.t: Et nunc non eis sufficit, quod durissima nos opprimunt servitute in captivitate, quæ est mors civilis; sed robur manuum suarum, idolorum potentiæ deputantes, id est potestatem quam habent a te Deo vero, a quo omnis potestas, suis diis atque simulacris adscribentes tanquam datoribus potestatis,
paras.en: [[14:8|And now they are not content to oppress us with most hard bondage|Et nunc non eis sufficit, quod durissima nos opprimunt servitute]] in captivity, which is a civil death; [[14:8|but attributing the strength of their hands to the power of their idols|sed robur manuum suarum, idolorum potentiæ deputantes]], that is, ascribing the power which they have from thee, the true God, from whom is all power[[Rom 13:1||]], to their gods and images, as if these were the givers of power,

paras.t: volunt tua mutare promissa, id est, volunt nos privare tuæ pietatis effectibus, quos nobis pœnitentiam agentibus promisisti, dicens in Deuteronomio: Si ad cardines cæli fueris dissipatus, inde retrahet te Dominus Deus tuus, si conversus fueris ad eum in toto corde tuo; et delere hæreditatem tuam, id est, plebem Israeliticam omnino exstinguere, cujus posteritatem promisisti usque in finem sæculi conservare, dicens per Jeremiam: Hæc dicit Dominus, qui dat solem in lumine diei, ordinem lunæ et stellarum in lumine noctis: Si defecerint leges istæ coram me, et semen Israel deficiet, ut non sit gens coram me cunctis diebus: et claudere ora te laudantium, interficiendo tuos cultores; atque exstinguere gloriam templi et altaris tui, id est cultum sacrificiorum tuorum qui fit in templo tuo, et obsequium quod tibi ibidem impenditur, impedire: sicut tempore Judith Holofernes conatus est facere;
paras.en: [[14:9|They design to change thy promises|volunt tua mutare promissa]], that is, they wish to deprive us of the effects of thy mercy, which thou didst promise us when we do penance, saying in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 30:4|If thou be driven as far as the poles of heaven, the Lord thy God will fetch thee back from hence|Si ad cardines cæli fueris dissipatus, inde retrahet te Dominus Deus tuus]], if thou be converted to him with thy whole heart; [[14:9|and destroy thy inheritance|et delere hæreditatem tuam]], that is, utterly to blot out the people of Israel, whose posterity thou didst promise to preserve to the end of the world, saying by Jeremias: [[Jer 31:35|Thus saith the Lord, who giveth the sun for the light of the day, the order of the moon and of the stars, for the light of the night|Hæc dicit Dominus, qui dat solem in lumine diei, ordinem lunæ et stellarum in lumine noctis]]: [[Jer 31:36|If these ordinances shall fail before me|Si defecerint leges istæ coram me]], [[Jer 31:36|then also the seed of Israel shall fail, so as not to be a nation before me for ever|et semen Israel deficiet, ut non sit gens coram me cunctis diebus]]; [[14:9|and shut the mouths of them that praise thee|et claudere ora te laudantium]], by slaying thy worshippers; [[14:9|and extinguish the glory of thy temple and altar|atque exstinguere gloriam templi et altaris tui]], that is, hinder the worship of thy sacrifices which is offered in thy temple, and the service which is paid thee there: as Holofernes tried to do in the time of Judith[[Jdt 3:13||]];

paras.t: ut aperiant ora gentium, dando eis occasionem et materiam blasphemandi te et cærimonias tuas, et laudent idolorum fortitudinem, adscribendo eis victoriam qua prævalent nobis, quum tamen ex tua promissione, imo et efficientia id contingat propter nostra peccata, et prædicent carnalem regem in sempiternum, id est regem nos omnino exstinguentem et auferentem commendent perpetuo, et inter deos transferendum annuntient, tanquam qui optime fecerit nos tollendo, quia superstitiosos et turbatores pacis communis nos asserunt.
paras.en: [[14:10|That they may open the mouths of Gentiles|ut aperiant ora gentium]], giving them occasion and matter to blaspheme thee and thy ceremonies, [[14:10|and praise the strength of idols|et laudent idolorum fortitudinem]], ascribing to them the victory by which they prevail over us, though it comes about by thy permission, nay thy working, because of our sins, [[14:10|and magnify for ever a carnal king|et prædicent carnalem regem in sempiternum]], that is, praise for ever the king who utterly blots us out and takes us away, and proclaim that he is to be numbered among the gods, as one who did best in taking us away, since they say that we are superstitious and disturbers of the common peace.

paras.t: Ne tradas, Domine, sceptrum tuum, id est regiam potestatem super nos, his qui non sunt, id est impiis et sceleratissimis hominibus, qui protinus morientur, et spiritualiter nihil sunt, ac comparatione fidelium virtuosorumque hominum, nullius sunt momenti: secundum quod Apostolus ait, Qui se putat aliquid esse, quum nihil sit: ne rideant ad ruinam nostram; sed converte consilium eorum super eos, id est, læsionem quam suo consilio machinantur nobis infligere, fac eis infligi. Sic et Propheta oravit, Averte mala inimicis meis, in veritate tua disperde eos: ut impleatur in eis illud Ecclesiastici, Facienti nequissimum consilium, super ipsum devolvetur. Et eum qui cœpit in nos sævire, disperde, id est, ipsum Aman qui cœpit in nos crudelissime agere, contere. Hoc zelo justitiæ est petitum contra hostes boni communis atque divini cultus, et ut in præsenti puniantur, et per mortem sublati, cessent sibi damnationem peccando augere.
paras.en: [[14:11|Give not, O Lord, thy sceptre|Ne tradas, Domine, sceptrum tuum]], that is, royal power over us, [[14:11|to them that are not|his qui non sunt]], that is, to wicked and most criminal men, who will soon die, and who spiritually are nothing, and in comparison with faithful and virtuous men are of no account: according to what the Apostle says: [[Gal 6:3|if any man think himself to be some thing, whereas he is nothing|Qui se putat aliquid esse, quum nihil sit]]: [[14:11|lest they laugh at our ruin|ne rideant ad ruinam nostram]]; [[14:11|but turn their counsel upon themselves|sed converte consilium eorum super eos]], that is, the harm which by their counsel they scheme to inflict on us, make it be inflicted on them. So too the Prophet prayed: [[Ps 53:7|Turn back the evils upon my enemies; and cut them off in thy truth|Averte mala inimicis meis, in veritate tua disperde eos]]: that there may be fulfilled in them that saying of Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 27:30|A mischievous counsel shall be rolled back upon the author|Facienti nequissimum consilium, super ipsum devolvetur]]. [[14:11|and destroy him that hath begun to rage against us|Et eum qui cœpit in nos sævire, disperde]], that is, crush Aman himself, who has begun to deal most cruelly with us. This is asked out of zeal for justice against the enemies of the common good and of divine worship, both that they may be punished in this present life, and that, taken away by death, they may cease to increase their damnation by sinning.

paras.t: Memento, Domine, id est, per effectum declara te memorem nostri in bono, et ostende te nobis, per gratiosam exauditionem et illuminationem internam, in tempore tribulationis nostræ: sicut dixisti, Cum ipso sum in tribulatione: et da mihi fiduciam, id est mentis constantiam et confidentiam plenam in te, Rex Judæorum, qui tibi fideliter confitentur, et universæ, Domine, potestatis, id est dominator, dator et conservator omnium potestatum quæ respectu tuæ majestatis sunt servitutes et imbecillitates.
paras.en: [[14:12|Remember, O Lord|Memento, Domine]], that is, show by the effect that thou art mindful of us for good, [[14:12|and shew thyself to us|et ostende te nobis]] by gracious hearing and inward enlightenment, [[14:12|in the time of our tribulation|in tempore tribulationis nostræ]]: as thou hast said: [[Ps 90:15|I am with him in tribulation|Cum ipso sum in tribulatione]]: [[14:12|and give me boldness|et da mihi fiduciam]], that is, constancy of mind and full confidence in thee, King of the Jews [the Vulgate reads *rex deorum*, "king of gods"; the OCR here is unclear], who faithfully confess thee, [[14:12|and of all power|et universæ, Domine, potestatis]], that is, ruler, giver and preserver of all powers, which in respect of thy majesty are servitudes and weaknesses.

paras.t: Tribue sermonem compositum, id est ornatum ac audienti bene placentem, in ore meo: non ob laudem et gloriam meam, sed propter liberationem populi tui; in conspectu leonis, id est Assueri regis: qui ob eminentiam suæ potestatis ac regiæ dignitatis leo vocatur, et quia ex instigatione Aman crudele edictum contra Judæos emisit: et transfer cor illius in odium hostis nostri: ita ut odiat ipsum Aman, in quantum tam impius est, non in quantum est homo. Quod odium non est caritati contrarium: de quo fertur, Perfecto odio oderam illos. Ut et ipse pereat, id est, temporaliter puniatur per mortem, et ceteri qui ei consentiunt ad interficiendum nos: quoniam morte digni sunt, non ipse tantum, sed et consentientes eidem, quos ignorantia non excusat.
paras.en: [[14:13|Give me a well ordered speech|Tribue sermonem compositum]], that is, adorned and well pleasing to the hearer, [[14:13|in my mouth|in ore meo]], not for my own praise and glory but for the deliverance of thy people, [[14:13|in the presence of the lion|in conspectu leonis]], that is, of king Assuerus, who is called a lion because of the eminence of his power and royal dignity, and because at Aman's instigation he sent out a cruel edict against the Jews[[Esth 3:8||]]: [[14:13|and turn his heart to the hatred of our enemy|et transfer cor illius in odium hostis nostri]], so that he may hate Aman himself inasmuch as he is so wicked, not inasmuch as he is a man. Such hatred is not contrary to charity; of it is said: [[Ps 138:22|I have hated them with a perfect hatred|Perfecto odio oderam illos]]. [[14:13|that both he himself may perish|Ut et ipse pereat]], that is, be punished in time by death, [[14:13|and the rest that consent to him|et ceteri qui ei consentiunt]] to kill us: since they are worthy of death, not he only but those also who consent to him[[Rom 1:32||]], whom ignorance does not excuse.

paras.t: Adjuva me ancillam tuam, nullum aliud auxilium habentem, nisi te, Domine, qui habes omnium scientiam, et nosti quia oderim gloriam iniquorum, id est vanam eorum gloriationem, ambitionem, jactantiam, et detester cubile incircumcisorum et omnis alienigenæ, id est idololatræ, sicut lex continet, et quantum in me est, quamvis propter rationabiles causas illud admittam.
paras.en: [[14:14|help me|Adjuva me]] thy handmaid, [[14:14|who have no other helper, but thee, O Lord, who hast the knowledge of all things|nullum aliud auxilium habentem, nisi te, Domine, qui habes omnium scientiam]], [[14:15|And thou knowest that I hate the glory of the wicked|et nosti quia oderim gloriam iniquorum]], that is, their vain boasting, ambition and display, [[14:15|and abhor the bed of the uncircumcised, and of every stranger|et detester cubile incircumcisorum et omnis alienigenæ]], that is, idolater, as the law has it[[Deut 7:3||]], and as far as lies in me, although for reasonable causes I admit it.

paras.t: Ideo additur: Tu scis infirmitatem meam, quia per me, sine favore regis, nequeo plebi meæ succurrere; et necessitatem meam, qua compellor regi misceri: quæ in hoc conjugio causa est dispensationis: et quod abominer signum superbiæ et gloriæ meæ, quod est super caput meum, id est regium diadema, quod est signum excellentiæ atque honoris mei, in diebus ostentationis meæ, quando procedo in publicum, ut ostendatur populo pulchritudo et eminentia mea; et detester illud quasi pannum menstruatæ: quo quid sordidius invenitur? et non portem illud in diebus silentii mei; dum permittor in secreto thalami mei Deo vacare in tranquillitate, silentio et contemplatione, quoniam femineam quoque loquacitatem abhorreo:
paras.en: Therefore it is added: Thou knowest my weakness [Denis reads *infirmitatem*], that by myself, without the king's favour, I cannot help my people; and [[14:16|my necessity|et necessitatem meam]], by which I am compelled to be joined to the king: which is the cause of the dispensation in this marriage [that is, of its being allowed though against the law]; [[14:16|that I abominate the sign of my pride and glory, which is upon my head|et quod abominer signum superbiæ et gloriæ meæ, quod est super caput meum]], that is, the royal diadem, which is the sign of my excellence and honour, [[14:16|in the days of my public appearance|in diebus ostentationis meæ]], when I go forth in public so that my beauty and eminence may be shown to the people; [[14:16|and detest it as a menstruous rag|et detester illud quasi pannum menstruatæ]]: than which what is found more filthy? [[14:16|and wear it not in the days of my silence|et non portem illud in diebus silentii mei]], while I am allowed in the secret of my chamber to give myself to God in tranquillity, silence and contemplation, for I abhor womanish talkativeness too:

paras.t: et quod non comederim in mensa Aman, eundo ad ejus convivia, sicut frequenter optavit, quamvis ex necessaria causa bis invitaverim eum ad mensam meam; nec mihi placuerit convivium regis: propter cibos qui in eo ponuntur, lege prohibitos, et propter varias pompas, dissolutiones et apparatus ibi admixtos: et non biberim vinum libaminum, id est sacrificiorum, videlicet vinum idolis immolatum;
paras.en: [[14:17|And that I have not eaten at Aman's table|et quod non comederim in mensa Aman]], by going to his banquets, as he often wished, although for a necessary cause I twice invited him to my table[[Esth 5:4||]][[Esth 5:8||]]; [[14:17|nor hath the king's banquet pleased me|nec mihi placuerit convivium regis]], because of the foods set out at it which the law forbids, and because of the various pomps, dissipations and display mingled there: [[14:17|and that I have not drunk the wine of the drink offerings|et non biberim vinum libaminum]], that is, of sacrifices, namely wine offered to idols;

paras.t: et nunquam lætata sit ancilla tua, ex quo huc translata sum a terra Babylonis (ut dictum est ante), nisi in te, Domine, Deus Abraham: qui licet sis omnium Deus, tamen ad Moysen es locutus: Hæc dices filiis Israel: Deus Abraham, Deus Isaac, et Deus Jacob misit me ad vos. Hoc nomen est mihi in æternum.
paras.en: [[14:18|And that thy handmaid hath never rejoiced, since I was brought hither|et nunquam lætata sit ancilla tua, ex quo huc translata sum]] from the land of Babylon (as was said before[[Esth 2:6||]]), [[14:18|but in thee, O Lord, the God of Abraham|nisi in te, Domine, Deus Abraham]]: who, though thou art the God of all[[Acts 10:36||]], yet didst speak to Moses: [[Ex 3:15|Thus shalt thou say to the children of Israel|Hæc dices filiis Israel]]: [[Ex 3:15|the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob hath sent me to you|Deus Abraham, Deus Isaac, et Deus Jacob misit me ad vos]]; [[Ex 3:15|this is my name for ever|Hoc nomen est mihi in æternum]].

paras.t: Deus fortis super omnes: quia solus omnipotens, et infinite universis potentior; exaudi vocem eorum qui nullam aliam spem habent, quam in te, seu nullum in quo confidant, nisi te, Domine; et erue me a timore meo, id est a periculo quod timeo, et ab isto timore quo affligor.
paras.en: [[14:19|O God, who art mighty above all|Deus fortis super omnes]]: because thou alone art almighty, and infinitely mightier than all things; [[14:19|hear the voice of them, that have no other hope|exaudi vocem eorum qui nullam aliam spem habent]] but in thee, or none in whom they trust but thee, O Lord; [[14:19|and deliver me from my fear|et erue me a timore meo]], that is, from the peril which I fear, and from this fear by which I am afflicted.

paras.t: Ecce quam devota, fervens et profunda oratio: et o quanta ex his probatur fuisse hujus electæ reginæ perfectio, quæ in tanta opulentia, honorificentia et frequentia constituta, tam virtuose, timorate et ordinate se habuit; quæ omnem gloriam mundi, voluptatem, dignitatem, vanitatesque sæculi tam plenissime sprevit, ita ut nunquam nisi in Deo sit gloriata in regali palatio! Nonne Spiritus ubi vult spirat, et Omnipotens corda suorum ubique juxta placitum suum immutat, afficit et gubernat? Quid ad hæc nos pusilli dicemus, qui ex levi et volatili verbo, signo aut facto inaniter gloriamur aut pueriliter conturbamur, et sumus ut pulvis quem projicit ventus a facie terræ? Instruamur ergo perfectione virtutum feminæ hujus sanctæ; et qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur. Nec ostentari, apparere, famari optemus, neque in vestitu aut ornamentis unquam lætemur. In omni quoque tribulatione confugiamus ad Deum, et reos nos esse ex cordis intima compunctione confiteamur, ac divinam commendemus justitiam. Postremo, quod sancta hæc Esther sic commemorat suas virtutes, fecit ad Dei honorem et nostram ædificationem, præsertim ad augendam confidentiam suam in Deo.
paras.en: Behold how devout, fervent and deep a prayer! And O how great the perfection of this chosen queen is proved by these things to have been, who, set amid such wealth, honour and throng, bore herself so virtuously, so God-fearingly and so orderly; who so utterly despised all the glory of the world, its pleasure, its dignity and the vanities of the age, that she never gloried in the royal palace except in God! Is it not so, that [[John 3:8|The Spirit breatheth where he will|Spiritus ubi vult spirat]], and that the Almighty everywhere changes, moves and governs the hearts of his own according to his good pleasure? What shall we little ones say to this, who glory vainly or are childishly troubled at a light and fleeting word, sign or deed, and are [[Ps 1:4|like the dust, which the wind driveth from the face of the earth|ut pulvis quem projicit ventus a facie terræ]]? Let us then be instructed by the perfection of the virtues of this holy woman; and [[2 Cor 10:17|he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord|qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur]][[1 Cor 1:31||]]. Let us not desire to be shown off, to be seen, to be talked of, nor ever rejoice in clothing or ornaments. In every tribulation also let us flee to God, and confess with inmost compunction of heart that we are guilty, and praise the divine justice. Lastly, that holy Esther thus recounts her virtues, she did for God's honour and our edification, and especially to increase her own confidence in God.
